signals.name: 'Ghadir' OTH Radar
signals.description: 'Ghadir', is an Iranian over the horizon radar, part of Iran's Sepehr Phased Radar System.

signals.name: 'OTH-SW' OTH Radar
signals.description: OTH-SW is a Chinese over-the-horizon radar. It is known to operate with pulse repetition frequencies of 43 Hz and 86 Hz.

signals.name: 'Vario' Airplane Data Controller
signals.description: This transmitter is found within the UHF FMRS bands, most likely used at airshows to give off barometric pressure, height in altitude represented by a voice, including various tones representing how high/how low the model plane is in the air.

signals.name: 17067bps FSK
signals.description: Unknown military-use signal reminiscent of [[Motorola SECURENET|SECURENET]] CVSD voice.

signals.name: 1G (NMT) Nordic Mobile Telephone
signals.description: Nordic Mobile Telephone (NMT, NMT-450, and NMT-900) is a first generation analog cell phone system. Originally designed for and by Nordic countries (Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark) it was widely deployed around the world. Nowadays (as of 2015) NMT is defunct.

signals.name: 1G Advanced Mobile Phone System (AMPS)
signals.description: The first generation of cellular mobile telecommunications, which used analogue NFM voice.

signals.name: 2006 Kia Grand Carnival Keyfob
signals.description: Original remote of KIA Carnival (2006).

signals.name: 29B6 'Kontayner' OTH Radar
signals.description: 29B6, nicknamed 'Контейнер' (Kontayner), is a Russian over the horizon radar. It is currently very active in Europe. signals.name: 2G (GSM) Global System for Mobile Communications
signals.description: GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) is a standard developed by ETSI to describe the protocols for second-generation (2G) digital cellular networks used by mobile phones. As of 2014, it has become the default global standard for mobile communications.

signals.name: 2G CDMA (IS-95)
signals.description: CDMA-One also known as IS-95, was the first ever cellular standard technology based on Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA). It is a predecessor of the 1xRTT (CDMA2000/IS-2000) standard, which is backwards compatible.

signals.name: 3G WCDMA
signals.description: WCDMA, known primarily as 3G mobile, is a family of 3G data protocols used to send voice, text and signaling data to smart phones and other wireless devices.

signals.name: 406 MHz Distress Beacon
signals.description: COSPAS-SARSAT 406 MHz emergency locator transmitters.

signals.name: 49MHz RC Car Controller
signals.description: The sound of an RC controller signal from an old amphibious toy car

signals.name: 4G (LTE) Long Term Evolution Uplink
signals.description: Acquired via telecommunications carrier hardware during interference investigation of an Australian cellular network.

signals.name: 4G LTE Network
signals.description: Long Term Evolution Network. Also known as 4G LTE Data and Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (E-UTRA). Data service for wireless consumer devices.

signals.name: 4G LTE450
signals.description: LTE 450 refers to the deployment of Long-Term Evolution (LTE) technology in the 380-512 MHz frequency band. LTE 450 networks allow various 4G LTE options to deliver efficient and reliable telecommunications services: LTE, LTE-M, and NB-IoT.

signals.name: 5G 'New Radio' Cellular Radio - Downlink
signals.description: 5G cellular, also known by 3GPP '5G' NR (new radio), etc. is a newly released cellular standard that allows for backwards compatibility with 4G LTE, and will allow for several gigabits of connection speeds, (up to 10-100Gb) per second. This is the 600 MHz downlink band for the ne

signals.name: 5G (NR) New Radio Uplink
signals.description: 5G cellular, also known by 3GPP '5G' NR (new radio), etc. is a newly released cellular standard that allows for backwards compatibility with 4G LTE, and will allow for several gigabits of connection speeds, (up to 10-100Gb) per second. This is the 600 MHz downlink band for the ne

signals.name: 5G Broadcast (MBMS) Multimedia Broadcast / Multicast Service
signals.description: A technology originally introduced in LTE (eMBMS) that enables efficient transmission of the same content to a large number of users at once — that is, broadcast or multicast instead of individual unicast. In 5G, its evolution is used for the so‑called LTE‑based 5G Terrestrial Br

signals.name: 77Ya6 'Voronezh' radar
signals.description: Voronezh (Воронеж) is a Russian radar family capable of aircraft and ballistic missile monitoring.

signals.name: 800 MHz Trunked Radio
signals.description: Public-safety and commercial trunked FM/digital systems.

signals.name: 802.11ah
signals.description: HaLow (802.11ah) is a wireless technology standard for exchanging data between devices over medium distances. Released by the Wi-Fi Alliance in 2016, it was initially developed as a competitive Internet of Things standard.

signals.name: 802.11ax
signals.description: IEEE 802.11ax-2021, also known as Wi-Fi 6, is a WLAN standard improves upon previous Wi-Fi standards by utilizing 1024QAM modulation, larger channel bandwidths, and improved efficiency.

signals.name: 802.11n
signals.description: IEEE 802.11n-2009, commonly shortened to 802.11n, is a wireless-networking standard that uses multiple antennas to increase data rates. The Wi-Fi Alliance has also retroactively labeled the technology for the standard as Wi-Fi 4.

signals.name: 8PSK
signals.description: 8PSK modulation is a way to encode data using eight phase angles. Each symbol can encode three bits of data. It can achieve higher data rates than other phase modulation schemes, but it also requires a higher signal-to-noise ratio and is more prone to errors.

signals.name: Accurate positioning by Low Frequencies (ALF)
signals.description: Accurate positioning by Low Frequencies, a former German DGPS navigation system. No longer in use as of 2013.

signals.name: Acer X222W monitor, sleep pulse
signals.description: Used for some PC monitors to keep the monitor's power on (or sleeping) across the spectra. Monitors may transmit whatever frequency peaks needed to keep it "on" or on sleep mode.

signals.name: AFSK Paging Link
signals.description: A variant of POCSAG/FLEX with audio FSK modulation based off of the bell 202 tones. Typically found as uplinks/downlinks to pager network transmitters.

signals.name: Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS)
signals.description: ACARS is a digital datalink system for the transmission of short messages between aircraft and ground stations via airband radio or satellite.

signals.name: AIST 2D
signals.description: Aist 2D is a Russian microsatellite developed and designed by a group of Samara Aerospace University students, postgraduates, and scientists in cooperation with TsSKB-Progress.

signals.name: AKKORD-SS-PD
signals.description: Akkord-SS-PD (АККОРД-СС-ПД), also known as “Akkord-165” is a Russian datalink used during the invasion of Ukraine. Akkord is a rather old family of datalink protocols, Akkord-165 being the most recent version.

signals.name: ALE-400
signals.description: ALE-400 is an amateur version of the 2G ALE standard. It is adapted to the demands of amateur radio emergency traffic handling.

signals.name: Alps Electric Co. TWB1U840 Key Fob
signals.description: Alps Electric Co. TWB1U840 Key Fob for Nissan Sentra, Nissan Versa, and Nissan Leaf model years 2013-2017+.

signals.name: Altai Radiotelephone
signals.description: The initial generation of cellular mobile radiotelecommunications, similar to trunked radio.

signals.name: AM Broadcast
signals.description: Medium-wave amplitude-modulated broadcast radio.

signals.name: Amateur 2 m FM
signals.description: 144–148 MHz narrowband FM voice and repeaters.

signals.name: Amateur 70 cm FM
signals.description: 420–450 MHz narrowband FM voice and repeaters.

signals.name: Amateur CW / Morse
signals.description: On-off keyed Morse in HF CW segments.

signals.name: Amateur HF SSB
signals.description: HF single-sideband voice on amateur allocations.

signals.name: Amplitude Modulation (AM)
signals.description: Long range commercial broadcast and international radio. Also used for aviation communications.

signals.name: Amplitude Modulation Signalling System (AMSS)
signals.description: Amplitude Modulation Signalling System (AMSS) is a DRM-based radiotext and data technology for AM broadcasting, like RDS that is used for FM. It transmits as a subcarrier, phase-modulating the carrier frequency.

signals.name: AMSAT-P3D
signals.description: AMSAT-P3D (Known as Phase 3D, OSCAR-40, and AO-40) is a amateur radio satellite built by AMSAT. As of 2004, the satellite's systems have failed.

signals.name: Aprizesat
signals.description: Data downlink from Aprizesat microsatellites. Aprizesat constellation consists of 12 Active satellites, These provide a worldwide M2M asset tracking service and relay AIS packets.

signals.name: Aqua Direct Broadcast (DB)
signals.description: A direct broadcast sent in the X band by the NASA Aqua satellite for reception by end users.

signals.name: ARGOS A-DCS
signals.description: Some polar weather satellites from the METOP and POES series carry ARGOS A-DCS (Advanced Data Collection System), which is a system to collect data from sondes and other remote land or air-based instrumentation.

signals.name: ARQ-E(E3)
signals.description: ARQ-E, also known as ARQ-1000 Duplex or ARQ-1000D, is a synchronous full-duplex ARQ system. ARQ-E3 is a variant that uses a different alphabet encoding. Mainly used by French Military Forces. Stations commonly idled for hours on end.

signals.name: ARQ-M2-242
signals.description: ARQ-M2-242 (Also known as TDM 242, TDM-2, 96-TDM, and ARQ-28) is a two-channel time division multiplexed telex system. This is the CCIR 242 standard version. Used in Aeronautical, Marine, and Point-to-Point services.

signals.name: ARQ-M2-342
signals.description: ARQ-M2-342 (Also known as TDM 342, TDM-2, 96-TDM, and ARQ-28) is a two-channel time division multiplexed telex system. This is the CCIR 342 standard version. Used in Aeronautical, Maritime, and Point-to-Point services.

signals.name: ARQ-M4-242
signals.description: ARQ-M4-242 (Also known as TDM 242, TDM-4, 192-TDM, and ARQ-56) is a four-channel time division multiplexed telex system. This is the CCIR 242 standard version. Used in Aeronautical, Maritime, and Point-to-Point services.

signals.name: ARQ-M4-342
signals.description: ARQ-M4-342 (Also known as TDM 342, TDM-4, 192-TDM, and ARQ-56) is a four-channel time division multiplexed telex system. This is the CCIR 342 standard version. Used in Aeronautical, Maritime, and Point-to-Point services.

signals.name: ARQ-N
signals.description: ARQ-N is a synchronous dual channel ARQ mode identical to ARQ-E, with the only difference being that ARQ-N has no symbol inversions. Formerly used by Italian Diplomatic services.

signals.name: ARQ6-90
signals.description: ARQ6-90, also known as ARQ-6-90 and ARQ-6/90, is a 6-character block simplex ARQ system formerly used by French and Italian diplomatic services exchange of teletype-data. It is no longer used or seen today.

signals.name: ARQ6-98
signals.description: ARQ6-98, also known as ARQ-6-98 and ARQ-6/98, is a 6-character block simplex ARQ system formerly used by French and Italian diplomatic services for the exchange of teletype-data. It is no longer used or seen today.

signals.name: ASCII
signals.description: ASCII (also known as ITA5 or IRA) is an amateur radio telegraphy signal using the ITA-5 alphabet.

signals.name: ATSC Broadcast
signals.description: Advanced Television Systems Committee Television. 8VSB Modulation

signals.name: AUDI keyfob
signals.description: Audi keyfobs transmit encrypted, short radio bursts that carry authentication data to the vehicle. signals.name: Autocab
signals.description: This is an example of the Autocab Media Data Terminals used by cab companies all over the world.

signals.name: Automated Train Control System (ATCS)
signals.description: Automated Train Control System (ATCS), specifically ATCS Spec. 200, is a standardized communication system for railroads designed to ensure safety by monitoring locations of trains and locomotives, providing analysis and reporting, and automation of track warrants and similar ord

signals.name: Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B)
signals.description: ADS-B is used by aircraft as an alternative to secondary radar. It broadcasts GPS position (latitude, longitude), pressure altitude, callsign, as well as track and ground speed.

signals.name: Automatic Identification System (AIS)
signals.description: Automatic Identification System (AIS) is used by ships to broadcast position and vessel information.

signals.name: Automatic Link Establishment (2G ALE)
signals.description: Automatic Link Establishment, 2G ALE (Official designation MIL-STD-188-141A and/or MIL-STD-188-141B (Appendix A)) is the current standardized method of establishing connections between radio operators. Also known as FED-STD 1045, FED-STD 1049, and STANAG 5066.

signals.name: Automatic Link Establishment (3G ALE ARCS)
signals.description: 3G ALE (ARCS) is the next generation of ALE (Designated by MIL-STD-188-141B (Appendix C)). Also known as STANAG 4538, although MIL 188-141 does not provide Fast LSU.

signals.name: Automatic Link Establishment (4G ALE WALE)
signals.description: 4G ALE (Wideband ALE, WALE), defined by MIL-STD-188-141D Appendices G and H. signals.name: Automatic Link Set-up (ALIS)
signals.description: Automatic Link Set-up (ALIS) is an automatic link system used by Rohde & Schwarz modems.

signals.name: Automatic Packet Reporting System (APRS)
signals.description: Packet system for real time data communications. Used by hams for location reporting, weather stations etc.

signals.name: Automatic Picture Transmission (APT)
signals.description: Automatic Picture Transmission (APT), also known as NOAA-GEOSAT, was an analog image transmission mode used by the NOAA weather satellites and some Russian weather satellites to transmit satellite weather photos. As of august 2025, most of the NOAA sats that transmitted this mode

signals.name: Automatic Transmitter Identification System (ATIS)
signals.description: ATIS systems are identification tags used by inland commercial waterway traffic on rivers in Europe. The FSK burst is appended at the end of every voice transmission by the vessel operator.

signals.name: AUTOSPEC
signals.description: AUTOSPEC is a synchronous FEC teletype system used by British coastal stations to communicate with North Sea oil rigs. Also known as Autospec-bauer, Bauer, and Autospec Mk1. This signal is most likely phased out.

signals.name: B-Netz
signals.description: B-Netz, was an analog, commercial mobile radio telephone network that was operated by the Deutsche Bundespost in Germany (at first only West Germany) from 1972 until 1994. The system was also implemented in neighboring countries Austria, The Netherlands and Luxembourg.

signals.name: BALDR Weather Sensor Telemetry
signals.description: BalDR weather sensor SCADA telemetry, A signal standard that belongs to the BalDR brand of weather sensors, and might also belong to other brands of weather sensors that use their technologies. Uses a set of randomly-generated delimiters which vary the overall pitch of the signal

signals.name: Baofeng GMSK
signals.description: Proprietary GMSK mode used for voice by Fujian Baofeng walkie talkies

signals.name: Beta
signals.description: Beta is the designation of a time signal service which is transmitted from multiple Russian VLF stations.

signals.name: Binary Interchange of Information and Signaling (BIIS)
signals.description: BIIS (also known as BIIS 1200) is an ETSI protocol for a digital selective calling method with the added benefit of extended capability of transmitting data that exceeds what could be done with old 5-tone analog calling methods like CCIR and ZVEI.

signals.name: Bluetooth
signals.description: Bluetooth is a wireless technology standard for exchanging data over short distances from fixed and mobile devices and building personal area networks (PANs). Invented by telecom vendor Ericsson in 1994, it was initially conceived as a wireless alternative to RS-232 data cables.

signals.name: Bluetooth Low Energy
signals.description: Bluetooth Low Energy - uses the same 2.400–2.4835 GHz ISM band as classic [Bluetooth](https://www.sigidwiki.com/wiki/Bluetooth) - is NOT backward-compatible with classic Bluetooth (Basic Rate/Enhanced Rate). - devices can have either classic Bluetooth, Bluetooth LE or both. - BLE

signals.name: BlueWalker-3 Wideband Telemetry
signals.description: Wideband telemetry signal from BlueWalker-3 experimental satellite.

signals.name: BMW Key-Code signal
signals.description: This coded signal was sent by BMW Car-Key. It is used to open and lock bimmer doors.

signals.name: BPC
signals.description: BPC is the callsign of the Chinese low-frequency time broadcasting station, located near Shangqiu, Henan in China.

signals.name: BPM
signals.description: BPM is a time signal transmitted by the Chinese Academy of Sciences, broadcasting from CAS's National Time Service Center in Pucheng County, China.

signals.name: BR-6028
signals.description: BR-6028 is a VFT (Voice Frequency Telegraph) frequency and time diversity modem using 7 data channels. It is sometimes also known as BARRIE, USA-7, or 6028.

signals.name: BRAS-3 (RS-10)
signals.description: BRAS-3 and the closely related RS-10 are Russian medium frequency hyperbolic navigation systems used for marine navigation

signals.name: Broadband Global Area Network (BGAN)
signals.description: Proprietary satellite network owned and operated by Inmarsat that provides cellular 3G equivalent data and voice services to subscribers.

signals.name: Canadian Meteor Orbit Radar (CMOR)
signals.description: Canadian Meteor Orbit Radar, or CMOR, is a meteor detection radar located near Tavistock, Ontario.

signals.name: CAS-4A/B Satellite Telemetry
signals.description: CAS-4A/B Satellite 4.8 kbps GMSK Telemetry Downlink.

signals.name: CB Radio
signals.description: 27 MHz Citizens Band AM/SSB voice.

signals.name: CBET
signals.description: CBET "Critical Band Encoded Tones" are tones added into radio broadcast's audio output for identification purposes.

signals.name: CCIR 493-4 Selcall
signals.description: CCIR 493-4 Selcall, also known as HF Selcall, Australian Selcall, and Codan 8580 Selcall, is a Selcall standard developed in Australia for the HF band. Used by Amateur radio and Codan Modems.

signals.name: CCIR Selcall
signals.description: CCIR selcall consists of CCIR-1, CCIR-2, and PCCIR, which are 5-tone selcall modes for VHF/UHF radios. CCIR-1 and CCIR-2 only differ in the tone duration, and PCCIR only differs in the group, reset, and repeat tone frequencies.

signals.name: CCITT
signals.description: CCITT is a 5-tone selcall system for VHF/UHF radios.

signals.name: CDMA2000 (3G physical layer)
signals.description: CDMA2000, or IS-2000, is a cellular network standard utilizing the CDMA technology for calls and data.

signals.name: Chilean Naval Time Signal
signals.description: Naval VHF time signal found in Chilean Coast, in Vina Del Mar

signals.name: China digital radio (CDR)
signals.description: Convergent Digital Radio (CDR) or China Digital Radio is an in-band-on-channel (IBOC) digital radio broadcasting format used in China. It can be found in multiple bandwidth configurations with different modulation formats.

signals.name: Chinese 'Foghorn' OTH radar
signals.description: A Chinese over the horizon radar, known as "foghorn" among amateur radio operators. Not much is known about it.

signals.name: Chinese 160kHz-wide OTH radar
signals.description: Chinese OTH radar with wide bandwidth and usually low sweep rate. Little information is available.

signals.name: Chinese 30-tone OFDM modem
signals.description: A 30-tone OFDM data mode, probably used by Chinese military or other agencies.

signals.name: Chinese 4+4
signals.description: Chinese 4+4, also known as 4+4 or PRC 4+4, is a multi-carrier transmission mode. It used by Chinese Diplomatic services with most traffic originating from Beijing, China.

signals.name: Chinese Firedrake Jammer
signals.description: Commercial AM Broadcast jamming signal that plays Chinese folk songs to jam specific radio stations in Asia from being received by listeners.

signals.name: Chinese Multitonal Jammer
signals.description: Chinese radio jamming signals intended to disrupt/censor broadcast communications.

signals.name: Chinese-64 MFSK
signals.description: Chinese Modem MFSK-64

signals.name: Chinese/Asian radio "MDC1200"
signals.description: Chinese radios failing to mimic mdc1200 or produces really old mdc1200 sound.

signals.name: CHIP
signals.description: CHIP is a spread-spectrum PSK mode developed by Antonino Porcino IZ8BLY. CHIP-64 runs at 37.5 bps, whereas CHIP-128 runs at 21.09 bps.

signals.name: CHU
signals.description: CHU was a time signal radio station operated by the Institute for National Measurement Standards of the National Research Council of Canada.

signals.name: CIS 3x100 VFT
signals.description: Three CIS-14 signals overlaid on top of each other in a 3100 Hz VFT bandwidth, operating at 100 bd

signals.name: CIS 3x144 VFT
signals.description: Three 144 Bd FSK signals in a 3100 Hz VFT bandwidth. Reportedly phased out.

signals.name: CIS 3xBaudot-50 VFT
signals.description: Three 50 bd Baudot signals in a 3100 Hz VFT bandwidth.

signals.name: CIS FTM-4
signals.description: CIS FTM-4 is the unofficial designation of a four-tone MFSK data mode which is apparently used by Russian military.

signals.name: CIS MFSK-11
signals.description: This MSFK-11 signal is widely believed to originate from Russia, used by Russian intelligence, military or diplomatic agencies.

signals.name: CIS MFSK-16 XPA2
signals.description: Enigma Designation XPA2, also known as MFSK-16, CIS MFSK-14, and CIS MFSK-16, is a 14-tone MFSK signal said to have origin from Russian Intelligence and Foreign Ministry stations.

signals.name: CIS MFSK-16 XPB
signals.description: Enigma designation XPB is a custom 16-tone MFSK mode said to have origin from Russian Intelligence and Foreign Ministry stations.

signals.name: CIS MFSK-20 XPA
signals.description: Enigma Designation XPA, also known as MFSK-20, CIS MFSK-17, and CIS MFSK-20, is a 17-tone MFSK signal said to have origin from Russian Intelligence and Foreign Ministry stations.

signals.name: CIS MFSK-21-13
signals.description: An MFSK data mode that is believed to originate from Russian sources. Changes between MFSK-21, MFSK-13 and different speeds.

signals.name: CIS MFSK-68
signals.description: New Russian MFSK Modem that uses 68 MFSK (5 tones at a time) as well as a 9000 Bd 8-PSK insert every second which spans 10 kHz wide. This signal is often found attributed with CIS-3000, where CIS-3000 acts as the ALE for this signal as well as CIS-128. It is used by Russian diplo

signals.name: CIS OFDM HDR Modem
signals.description: Russian OFDM HDR (High Data Rate) Modem. Has three main modes: CIS-45, CIS-60, and CIS-93, corresponding to the number of OFDM tones in the signal.

signals.name: CIS OFDM-121
signals.description: CIS OFDM-121 is an OFDM mode that uses OFDM bursts with 121 channels, spaced by two QPSK-like bursts. Not all of the 121 available channels of OFDM bursts are used and it's possible to note a different arrangement of the channels in different days.

signals.name: CIS W-MFSK-17
signals.description: Presumably Russian MFSK signal with wide bandwidth and 17 tones

signals.name: CIS-11
signals.description: CIS-11 (Also known as TORG-11) is a radio duplex teleprinter system used by Russian meteorological stations

signals.name: CIS-112
signals.description: CIS-112 OFDM signal. Has a preamble of 7 Tones (not including carrier), then 56 tones before entering into the 112 tone data transmission.

signals.name: CIS-12
signals.description: CIS-12 (Also known as MS5, FIRE, AT-3004D, AT-3104D, T-230) is a 12-tone PSK Russian military multi-channel modem.

signals.name: CIS-1200 (T-230-1A 'Mahovik')
signals.description: CIS-1200, Mahovik, "Flywheel" in Russian, is a PSK based mode that can transmit both voice and data. It is transmitted from a Russian T-230-1A.

signals.name: CIS-128
signals.description: CIS-128 is an OFDM mode that uses 128 channels, with one “off” channel in the center, so the signal is divided into two 64 channel parts.

signals.name: CIS-1280
signals.description: CIS-1280 is a OQPSK (Offset Quadrature Phase Shift-Keying) modulation data modem signal. Also known as Soviet Mil(MOD)/FAPSI/PTT system. These stations are recognizable in that they are all placed on .081 offsets from a kilohertz or half kilohertz point.

signals.name: CIS-14
signals.description: Also known as AMOR and AMOR96. Synchronous FSK duplex teleprinter system with ARQ.

signals.name: CIS-16
signals.description: CIS-16 is a BPSK 16-tone mode, possibly transmitted from a modified AT-3004D or AT-3104 type Russian military transceiver. Also known as CIS 16x75 Bd for the 75 bd speed in each of the 16 sub channels.

signals.name: CIS-20
signals.description: Russian AT-3104 Modem signal, 20-tone OFDM DQPSK signal. Has characteristic pilot tone located 3300 Hz from suppressed carrier. All 20 channels operate at 75 Bd.

signals.name: CIS-300
signals.description: Known as CIS-300 Burst, FSK mode used with 300 Bd rate with a starting and ending tone on the upper part of the signal.

signals.name: CIS-3000
signals.description: CIS-3000 is an 8-PSK Data Modem protocol. Its source is traced to Russia. 3000 is for its 3000 Baud speed (maximum speed is technically 9000 bps).

signals.name: CIS-36-50
signals.description: CIS-36-50, also known as BEE-36, is an FSK modem used by the Russian Navy.

signals.name: CIS-40.5
signals.description: CIS-40.5 (Also known as T-206) is an FSK signal used in Russian Military Communications Equipment. Used as a telegraph channel, encrypted.

signals.name: CIS-48
signals.description: CIS-48 is an interesting data mode with a unique format. It uses a 4 DBPSK Preamble with a constant tone and changing OFDM modes as it transmits data. Origin is suspected to be in Russia.

signals.name: CIS-50-50
signals.description: CIS-50-50 is very similar to CIS-36-50. The main difference is in the available baud rates and frequency shifts used.

signals.name: CIS-8181
signals.description: CIS-8181 is an FSK modem used by the Russian navy.

signals.name: CLOUDSAT Downlink
signals.description: Dump to European ground station from the CLOUDSAT cloud profiling satellite. CLOUDSAT has a CPR (Cloud Profiling Radar) that operates at 94 GHz to create a vertical sounding (cross-section) of the atmosphere.

signals.name: CLOVER 2000
signals.description: CLOVER 2000 is an upgrade to CLOVER-II, a digital data protocol developed by Ray Petit and HAL Communications. Sometimes referred to as XCLOVER or 8 Tone CLOVER.

signals.name: CLOVER 2500
signals.description: CLOVER 2500 is a new upgrade to CLOVER-2000, adding 25% more speed to the CLOVER system.

signals.name: CLOVER-I
signals.description: CLOVER-I was the first iteration of the Clover series of digital modes. Was never released for commercial use, replaced by CLOVER-II. Also known as Cloverleaf.

signals.name: CLOVER-II
signals.description: CLOVER-II is the advancement of CLOVER-I, with 4 tone pulses and a max data rate of 750 bps. Also known as Q-CLOVER and QUAD-CLOVER.

signals.name: Cobra Dane
signals.description: The AN/FPS-108 COBRA DANE is a PESA phased array radar installation operated by Raytheon for the United States Space Force (originally for the United States Air Force) at Eareckson Air Station on the island of Shemya, Aleutian Islands, Alaska.

signals.name: Codan Data Modem
signals.description: Codan Data Modulation for Codan Data Modems. Has 3 distinct signals: Data, ALE, and SELCAL. This modulation is used in Codan's 9001, 9002, 3012 and 3212 modems.

signals.name: CODAR
signals.description: CODAR (Coastal Ocean Dynamics Applications Radar) is used for near-surface ocean monitoring, such as waves and water current.

signals.name: Coherent BPSK
signals.description: Coherent BPSK, also known as C-BPSK, was an experimental amateur mode developed by Bill DeCarle VE2IQ.

signals.name: Coherent CW
signals.description: Coherent CW (also known as CCW) was a strictly timed morse code mode designed by Ray Petit W7GHM (The same inventor of CLOVER). CCW depended on accurate timing from both receiver and transmitter.

signals.name: CompuLert
signals.description: Low speed FSK telemetry to monitor and control warning sirens that are used to warn the public of threats such as tsunamis, severe weather, chemical spills and civil emergencies.

signals.name: Contestia
signals.description: Contestia, developed by Nick Fedoseev (UT2UZ) in 2005, is a digital mode derived from Olivia. It aims to deliver a compromise of speed and performance.

signals.name: Continuous Tone-Coded Squelch System (CTCSS)
signals.description: CTCSS, also known as Private Line and Channel Guard, is a low continuous tone transmitted on NFM voice transmissions that is used to squelch and manage transmissions on a given frequency.

signals.name: Contrôle de vitesse par balises (KVB)
signals.description: "Speed control by beacons" railway safety system used in France and the Channel Tunnel line in the UK.

signals.name: Coquelet
signals.description: Coquelet is an MFSK system, similar to Piccolo. Also known as COQ-8, COQ-12, and COQUELET 8 V 2. Uses ITA-2 charset. It's two main modes are Coquelet-8 and Coquelet-13. No longer in use.

signals.name: CORIOLIS Tactical Direct Broadcast
signals.description: Direct Broadcast digital signal from the CORIOLIS satellite, primarily carries data from the WindSat instrument.

signals.name: CRY2001 Voice Scrambler
signals.description: CRY2001 is a voice scrambling mode used on Sailor CRY2001 Scramblers. Fisherman often use these modes to communicate with privacy.

signals.name: Cuban Jammer
signals.description: Cuban jammers jam the frequencies of Radio Martí, Radio Republica and occasionally WRMI radio.

signals.name: CV-786
signals.description: CV-786 is a wideband FSK mode built in Rockwell-Collins MDM-2001 modems. Also known as TRC-75, as it was used in TRC-75 transceivers. A military-based Radio TeleTYpe mode.

signals.name: D-STAR
signals.description: D-STAR is a digital voice protocol used by ham radio. Is sometimes routed over the internet for international communications.

signals.name: Datawell Buoy HF Link
signals.description: Datawell Buoy HF Links transmitted by Datawell Marine measurement buoys, measuring ocean conditions, temperature, and wave current.

signals.name: DB0UPB research beacon
signals.description: The is a research beacon for training neural networks.

signals.name: DCF77
signals.description: DCF77 is a German longwave time signal radio station based at 77.5 kHz. DCF uses an AM modulated carrier and phase modulation sidebands to transmit its time signal.

signals.name: Delfi-C3 Telemetry
signals.description: Delfi-C3 Telemetry was a telemetry signal sent from the Delfi-C3 university-class satellite.

signals.name: DeltaFix
signals.description: DeltaFix was a DGPS system that was used to provide precision positioning used in the survey and oceanographic industry.

signals.name: Denso 4EA Key Fob
signals.description: Denso Wireless Key Fob 4EA built by Denso Corporation for General Motors auto brands Chevrolet and Buick. Used on Chevrolet Camaro and Malibu from 2016+. Used on Buick Lacrosse 2017+.

signals.name: DFM-09
signals.description: GRAW DFM-09 radiosonde measures temperature, humidity, air pressure, wind direction, and wind speed.

signals.name: Differential Global Positioning System (DGPS)
signals.description: Differential GPS (DGPS), also known as M823 DGPS and SC-104 DGPS, is a supplementary correction signal used by GPS receivers to increase the accuracy of GPS based positioning.

signals.name: Digisonde
signals.description: Digisondes are ionosondes that use pulsed signal that can gather more radar information than a traditional ionosonde sweep.

signals.name: Digital Audio Broadcasting (DAB)
signals.description: DAB is an audio broadcasting standard containing a multiplex of digital radio stations in the signal.

signals.name: Digital Audio Broadcasting Plus (DAB+)
signals.description: DAB+ is a medium of delivering broadcast radio, containing multiple stations in a single multiplex.

signals.name: Digital Dispatch Systems MDT
signals.description: Digital Dispatch Systems Mobile Data Terminal is a dispatching system used by taxi and private transportation companies.

signals.name: Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications (DECT)
signals.description: DECT is a ETSI standard for short range communications, mainly cordless phones. It uses a 10 channel/24 slots in a TDMA FDD structure. Audio sample is 100 times slower than real for listening purposes.

signals.name: Digital Mobile Radio (DMR)
signals.description: Digital Mobile Radio (DMR) is an open digital mobile radio standard defined by ETSI and used in commercial products around the world. Mostly used by private network and local police, can be encrypted. Used in MOTOTRBO products.

signals.name: Digital Multimedia Broadcasting (DMB)
signals.description: Digital Multimedia Broadcasting (DMB) is a digital radio transmission technology developed in South Korea as part of the national IT project for sending multimedia such as TV, radio and datacasting to mobile devices such as mobile phones, laptops and GPS navigation systems.

signals.name: Digital NBTV
signals.description: Method for transmitting digital images via radio, similar to [[WinDRM]] or [[KG-STV]]

signals.name: Digital Private Mobile Radio (dPMR)
signals.description: dPMR is an open, non-proprietary trunked radio standard developed by ETSI, published under ETSI TS 102 658. Supports both data and digital voice transmission.

signals.name: Digital Radio Mondiale (DRM)
signals.description: Digital Radio Mondiale (DRM) is a digital commercial broadcasting mode used to deliver FM-comparable sound quality to shortwave radio.

signals.name: Digital Radio Mondiale Plus (DRM+)
signals.description: DRM+ is a VHF implementation of DRM primarily for the FM broadcast band.

signals.name: Digital Video Broadcasting — Cable (DVB-C)
signals.description: DVB‑C is a cable‑based digital TV transmission standard that delivers MPEG transport streams over coaxial networks using QAM modulation. It was first published as ETSI EN 300 429 and defines the framing, channel coding, and modulation needed for reliable multi‑program distributio

signals.name: Digital Video Broadcasting — Satellite (DVB-S)
signals.description: DVB‑S and DVB‑S2 are both satellite broadcasting standards, but DVB‑S2 is a more advanced and efficient evolution of the original system.

signals.name: Digital Video Broadcasting — Terrestrial (DVB-T)
signals.description: Digital Video Broadcasting — Terrestrial (DVB-T) is a digital broadcast television format used in Europe and in many other countries in the world.

signals.name: Digital-Coded Squelch (DCS)
signals.description: Digital in-band signalling used to squelch and manage transmissions on a given frequency.

signals.name: DisplayPort Interference
signals.description: DisplayPort is a digital standard used to carry video and audio data to computer monitors. It emits RF interference in the 300-400 MHz range when in use.

signals.name: Distress Radiobeacon (Analog)
signals.description: Analog Distress Radiobeacons are simple siren-based transmitters that were installed in older EPIRB's, PLB's and ELT's. Currently used as a supplementary homing signal in modern digital radiobeacons.

signals.name: Distress Radiobeacon (Digital)
signals.description: Digital Distress Radiobeacons (EPIRB's, PLB's and ELT's) are emergency radio beacons used for search and rescue operations to locate a vessel, plane, or person in distress.

signals.name: Distributed Power Unit (DPU)
signals.description: Distributed power refers to the placing of an extra locomotive at an intermediate point in the middle section of a train. This locomotive unit is remotely controlled from the lead locomotive, and greatly increases both the pulling and stopping power of longer trains.

signals.name: DominoEX
signals.description: DominoEX, also known as just Domino, is an IFK (Incremental Frequency Keying) mode developed by Murray Greenman ZL1BPU and Con Wassilieff ZL2AFP in 2004 that was the first fully developed iteration of the Domino IFK family modes. Used to send text over RF.

signals.name: DominoF
signals.description: DominoF was the first experimental implementation of the Domino family of IFK modes, developed by Con ZL2AFP. DominoF used dual interleaved tone sets. Superseded by DominoEX.

signals.name: Driftnet Buoy Radio Beacon
signals.description: Driftnet Radio Buoys are extensively used by fishing boats operating in open seas and oceans for collecting long fishing lines or fishing nets, with the assistance of a radio direction finder

signals.name: Dual Tone Multi Frequency (DTMF)
signals.description: DTMF is a signaling mode used for a variety of purposes. It's most known for telephony dialing, but is in use for many different applications such as DTMF paging for DTMF-enabled VHF/UHF radios.

signals.name: Duga radar
signals.description: Duga (Russian: Дуга́) Soviet over-the-horizon radar, now defunct

signals.name: DUP-ARQ
signals.description: DUP-ARQ, also known as ARTRAC and 125-ARTRAC, is a semi-duplex ARQ system once used by Thai and Hungarian Diplomatic services.

signals.name: DUP-ARQ-2
signals.description: DUP-ARQ-2 (also known as ARTRAC II) is a further development of the DUP-ARQ system and the system characteristics are very similar. DUP-ARQ-2 allows transmission of ITA-2 (Baudot) or ITA-5 (ASCII) characters depending on the application.

signals.name: DUP-FEC-2
signals.description: DUP-FEC-2 is a further development of the DUP-ARQ system and the system characteristics are very similar. Uses FEC instead of ARQ and runs at either 125 bd or 250 bd.

signals.name: EasyPal Digital SSTV
signals.description: Seen it on the Web-SDR Twente. It could be on any frequency. It's quite a short signal to contain a picture. signals.name: EBRO S800 keyfob
signals.description: The EBRO keyfob is a compact wireless remote used for vehicle access and basic control functions. signals.name: ECG Telemetry
signals.description: ECG Telemetry from a pacemaker.

signals.name: EEA
signals.description: EEA is a 5-tone selcall mode defined by the Electronic Engineering Association in the United Kingdom.

signals.name: EFR Teleswitch
signals.description: Europäische Funk-Rundsteuerung (EFR) Teleswitch (European Radio Ripple Control GmbH (ERA) Teleswitch) is an energy management system operated via long-wave radio. Uses two transmitters in Germany and one in Hungary. Also known by DCF39, DCF49 and HGA22.

signals.name: EIA
signals.description: EIA is a 5/6-tone selcall mode defined by the Electronics Industries Association in the United States. Also known as Motorola MetroPage.

signals.name: Electric Fence Remote Control
signals.description: This signal comes from an RF remote control device that transmits in UHF over 433.92MHz and controls the arming and disarming system of an electric fence.

signals.name: Électricité de France HNZ
signals.description: Electrical substation SCADA protocol used by EDF (Électricité de France).

signals.name: ELEKTRO-L GGAK-E Direct Broadcast
signals.description: Broadcasts the data from the GGAK-E cosmic ray detector onboard ELEKTRO-L geostationary weather satellites

signals.name: Emergency Alert System (EAS)
signals.description: The Emergency Alert System (EAS) is a national warning system in the United States, implemented since 1997, superceding the Emergency Broadcast System (EBS).

signals.name: Emergency Managers Weather Information Network (EMWIN) - Repeater
signals.description: The Emergency Managers Weather Information Network (EMWIN) is a system for distributing a live stream of weather information in the United States. This is the VHF Repeater of the network.

signals.name: End of Train Device (EOTD)
signals.description: Transmits train telemetry such as brake status and accidental separation information to the head locomotive.

signals.name: Enhanced Digital Access Communications System (EDACS)
signals.description: EDACS is a trunked radio system developed by General Electric and Ericsson. EDACS was invented by General Electric in the mid-80s and is currently owned by Harris Corporation. Harris has announced that EDACS systems will no longer be supported by 2017.

signals.name: Ethernet Over Powerline
signals.description: Ethernet Over Powerline, is an alternative way to reach ethernet cables through a set of adapters that go into outlets that can be plugged directly in the router instead of routing cables all the way from one end of a building to another. It creates the Pulse-Amplitude modulation

signals.name: EURO
signals.description: EURO is a 6/7-tone selcall mode used in VHF/UHF radios. Also known as EuroSignal.

signals.name: Eurobalise downlink
signals.description: Downlink from train to balise. A Eurobalise is a specific variant of a balise, a transponder placed between the rails of a railway.

signals.name: European Radio Message System (ERMES)
signals.description: European Radio Message System (ERMES) is a European common standard for paging developed by the European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ESTI)

signals.name: F03 numbers station
signals.description: Enigma designation F03 is a family of digital FSK modes, used by the "Polish 11" numbers station operator, which is likely a Polish intelligence agency.

signals.name: F07 number station
signals.description: F07 is a Russian digital number station known for using multiple modulation types, including MFSK, BPSK and FSK.

signals.name: FEC-A
signals.description: FEC-A, also known as FEC-100 or FEC-100A, is a synchronous simplex ARQ system that uses the ITA 2 alphabet. This mode was once used by many embassies, diplomatic services, and news agencies worldwide. This mode was developed by Siemens.

signals.name: Federal Signal Modem-MSK
signals.description: Signalling protocol developed for Federal Signal's various warning and mass notification appliances. This signal is used for activation and telemetry of all units in a network.

signals.name: FLASH-OFDM
signals.description: Fast Low-latency Access with Seamless Handoff Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (FLASH-OFDM) is a mobile data access technology developed by Flarion.

signals.name: FLEX
signals.description: FLEX (Flexible Wide Area Paging Protocol) is Motorola's high speed one-way paging protocol that supports 1600, 3200, and 6400 bps. FLEX can transmit tone, numeric, alphanumeric, and binary data.

signals.name: FLEX Paging
signals.description: Motorola FLEX multi-speed paging protocol.

signals.name: FM Broadcast
signals.description: Commercial and public wideband FM radio, 75–200 kHz deviation.

signals.name: FM Broadcast Radio
signals.description: Commercial Broadcast FM radio stations. Used for the broadcast of many different radio programs, including music, news, sports, weather, and talk shows.

signals.name: FM NBTV
signals.description: FM NBTV is a method to send moving images in a very narrow bandwidth (maximum 3 KHz)

signals.name: FreeDV COHPSK
signals.description: FreeDV Coherent PSK (Also known as FreeDV 700) is a robust Digital Voice mode developed by David Rowe for his FreeDV Digital Voice Software.

signals.name: FreeDV plus Video
signals.description: FreeDV plus Video (also known as FreeDV+) combines analog FM multicarrier Narrow Band TV (NBTV) by Con Wassilieff, ZL2AFP, and FreeDV digital voice by David Rowe, VK5DGR.

signals.name: Frequency Division Multiplex Digital Voice (FDMDV)
signals.description: Frequency Division Multiplex Digital Voice (FDMDV), also known as FDMDV 14+1-tone, is a digital voice mode originally developed by Peter Martinez G3PLX and Francesca Lanza HB9TLK. It has since been improved upon by David Rowe. ([[FreeDV COHPSK]])

signals.name: FRS / GMRS
signals.description: US Family Radio and General Mobile Radio Service FM.

signals.name: FSK441
signals.description: FSK441 is a high speed meteor scatter communication mode. FSK441 uses a baud rate of 441 Bd.

signals.name: FSQ
signals.description: Fast Simple QSO (FSQ) is an amateur radio digital modulation mode developed by Con Wassilieff ZL2AFP with Murray Greenman ZL1BPU in 2015.

signals.name: FST4
signals.description: FST4 is a 4-GFSK amateur radio communications mode, designed especially for making contacts (QSO's) on LF and MF frequency ranges under extreme weak-signal conditions. It is part of the WSJT-X software.

signals.name: FST4W
signals.description: FST4W is an amateur radio digital protocol designed particularly for the LF and MF bands, for quasi-beacon transmissions of WSPR-style messages. FST4W uses 4-GFSK modulation and offers T/R sequence lengths of 120, 300, 900, and 1800 seconds.

signals.name: FT4
signals.description: FT4 is an amateur radio contesting communication protocol developed by Joe Taylor (K1JT) and Steve Franke (K9AN) descended from FT8.

signals.name: FT8
signals.description: FT8 is an extremely-weak-signal amateur radio mode that transmits very limited communications. JS8, a variant of FT8, can send full conversations and relay messages

signals.name: FUNcube-1 Telemetry
signals.description: FUNcube-1 Telemetry is a telemetry signal sent from the Funcube-1 Cubesat amateur radio satellite.

signals.name: Futuba RC Controller
signals.description: 72-75 MHz transmitters are used to control various types of RC models. RC Controllers that use 72-75 MHz don't seem to be used as often as they used to.

signals.name: G-TOR
signals.description: Golay-Teleprinting Over Radio (G-TOR) is an FSK proprietary standard developed by Kantronics Inc. and is used by radio amateurs, military (Irish Air Corps/Navy, Mexican army) and governmental agencies (ICRC).

signals.name: Gandalf MDT
signals.description: Gandalf MDT was developed by Gandalf Mobile Systems, a subsidiary of Canadian company Gandalf Technologies. Used primarily by taxi and courier services in Canada and the United States. This protocol was used in Gandalf's Cabmate systems.

signals.name: Garage Door / Keyfob 315 MHz
signals.description: North American short-range ASK/OOK remotes.

signals.name: GK-2A LRIT ( Low-Rate Image Transmission )
signals.description: LRIT (Low-Rate Image Transmission) is used to transmit images on the GK-2A satellite

signals.name: Glenayre Paging Link
signals.description: Glenayre's Paging Link. With QAM being used, It is a way to upkeep a linked paging transmitter when no data is broadcast. Glenayre C2100/C2000 model control systems were likely to use this.

signals.name: Globe Wireless HF Network
signals.description: Globe Wireless' Maritime Digital Radio was a system of 24 stations around the globe offering data services to large cargo vessels. Since 2014, GW has discontinued their HF network.

signals.name: GM2100 (R&S)
signals.description: This is the proprietary HF Data Signal Protocol for the Rohde & Schwarz HF Modem GM2100.

signals.name: GMDSS Digital Selective Calling
signals.description: Global Maritime Distress and Safety System's Digital Selective Calling (GMDSS-DSC) is a maritime communication protocol intended to initiate ship-to-ship, ship-to-shore and shore-to-ship radiotelephone and MF/HF radiotelex calls.

signals.name: GOES CDA Telemetry
signals.description: Telemetry signal sent from GOES 16, 17 and 18. GOES is a family of Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite operated by the United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

signals.name: GOES Data Collection System (DCS)
signals.description: Comes from the geostationary satellites GOES 16 and GOES 17. Relays information about water levels, lightning strikes, and other information.

signals.name: GOES High Rate Information Transmission (HRIT)
signals.description: GOES HRIT is a retransmission of satellite imagery and other information from the GOES-R series of satellites.

signals.name: GOES HRIT / LRIT
signals.description: Geostationary weather satellite downlink near 1694 MHz.

signals.name: GOES Rebroadcast (GRB)
signals.description: GOES Rebroadcast (GRB) is a form of data sent from the GOES-R series of satellites that contain information from all of the instruments on board the GOES satellites

signals.name: Golay Paging (GSC)
signals.description: Golay Paging (or Golay Sequential Code, GSC) is a one-way 2-FSK paging format developed by Motorola. It is capable of transmitting tone, numeric, alphanumeric, and voice pages.

signals.name: Gonets
signals.description: Gonets (Russian Гонец, for Messenger) is a Russian civilian low Earth orbit communications satellite system.

signals.name: Google Pixel Interference
signals.description: 1.925hz pulsing signal (5 pulses) that repeats every few seconds around 5-10 times, then stops for an unknown period. Strong enough to completely disrupt AGC on CB band. Signal penetrates at most a few megahertz.

signals.name: GRAVES
signals.description: The Grand Réseau Adapté à la Veille Spatiale (GRAVES) system is a French space-surveillance system for low-orbit (up to 1000km) satellites. Emitter is based near Dijon, France.

signals.name: Graw DFM-06 Weather Balloon (Radiosonde)
signals.description: The DFM-06 is a standard radiosonde for most applications. It is perfectly suited for synoptic observations or military applications.

signals.name: GRAW DFM-09 Weather Balloon (Radiosonde)
signals.description: GRAW DFM-09 performs measurement of temperature, humidity, air pressure, wind direction and wind speed.

signals.name: Graw DFM-17 (Radiosonde)
signals.description: Radiosonde developed by Graw/Noris Group GmbH for upper air weather observation

signals.name: Grimeton Radio (SAQ)
signals.description: SAQ stands as the sole transmitter reliant on an alternating current generator. Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site, it employs the last operational Alexanderson alternator for RF production.

signals.name: Ground-Based Augmentation System (GBAS)
signals.description: GBAS is an advanced aircraft navigation system that provides GPS corrections to aircraft on approach.

signals.name: GYN2 GBR
signals.description: Transmitting site owned by the Ministry of Defense. Originally constructed in 1946 and was originally used as a shortwave radio station. signals.name: HC-265 Voice Scrambler
signals.description: HC-265 is a Voice Scrambling mode developed by Hagelin Crypto for their HC-265 CRYPTOCOM secure voice unit.

signals.name: HC-ARQ
signals.description: Haegelin Crypto ARQ (HC-ARQ) was an FSK synchronous simplex ARQ system used by the UN and International Rescue Committee. This mode has been phased out and is no longer in use.

signals.name: HD Radio (AM)
signals.description: HD Radio is a proprietary digital broadcast radio format transmitted in North America, usually as sidebands on analog carriers. This is the AM band implementation of HD Radio.

signals.name: HD Radio (FM)
signals.description: HD Radio is a proprietary digital broadcast radio format transmitted in North America, usually as sidebands on analog carriers. This is the FM band implementation of HD Radio.

signals.name: HDMI RFI Clock
signals.description: HDMI is a popular media source for delivering video, audio, all in the same stream. Unfortunately, there is massive interference from it when a neighboring SDR is near it. It can disrupt receiving to a great degree.

signals.name: Hellschreiber
signals.description: Hellschreiber (Also known as Feld Hell or just Hell) is a teleprinter system developed in the late 1920's by Rudolf Hell, a German inventor.

signals.name: HF Fax / Weatherfax
signals.description: Marine weather facsimile, FM on USB.

signals.name: HF trading link '120 Hz FMCW idle tone'
signals.description: A HF trading link in idle state which strongly resembles an FMCW radar with 120 Hz sweep rate. Has been observed to transmit CW ID once per hour.

signals.name: HFGCS (High Frequency Global Communications System)
signals.description: HFGCS is a series of networks deployed by the United States Air Force to send encoded messages to deployed aircraft. This network is well known for it's coded EAM's (Emergency Action Messages) used for coordinating United States Strategic Nuclear Forces.

signals.name: High Frequency Active Auroral Research Program (HAARP)
signals.description: HAARP is a ionospheric research program conducted in Gakona, Alaska.

signals.name: High Frequency Data and Voice Link (HFDVL)
signals.description: HFDVL (or HFD+VL) is an experimental mode developed by research groups from The University of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria and The Polytechnic University of Madrid. This mode is intended for military use in accordance with STANAG 5066 parameters.

signals.name: High Frequency Data Link (HFDL)
signals.description: HFDL, also known as HF-ACARS, ARINC 753, ARINC 635, and HF DATALINK,is a data link that aircraft use to communicate short messages over long distances using HF signals.

signals.name: High Power Auroral Stimulation (HIPAS)
signals.description: The HIPAS (HIgh Power Auroral Stimulation) Observatory was a research facility, built to study the ionosphere and its influence on radio communications. It was located 25 miles east of Fairbanks, Alaska in the Fairbanks North Star Borough area.

signals.name: High Resolution Data (HRD)
signals.description: The HRD direct broadcast is an X-band continuous downlink from NOAA JPSS satellites of mission environmental data to users on the ground that are equipped with a suitable receiver.

signals.name: High Speed USB Noise
signals.description: High Speed USB 2.0 clock noise. Shows up at multiples of 480 MHz.

signals.name: HNG-FEC
signals.description: HNG-FEC was a full duplex system developed and used solely by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Hungary. Used 100.05 bd with 500 Hz shift FSK. This mode is no longer used today.

signals.name: Hoffman Broadfield Signpost AVM System
signals.description: Proprietary FFSK data network used for public transport telemetry. It is primarily used to track and control vehicles, and facilitates PTT-ID for communication with tram drivers.

signals.name: Horus Binary 4FSK - v2
signals.description: An efficient RTTY-like 4FSK mode that transmits binary data, used for amateur high altitude balloon telemetry. Developed by the Project Horus group.

signals.name: HORYU-4 Telemetry
signals.description: Telemetry signal sent from the HORYU-4 university-class satellite Launched by Kyushu Institute of Technology in Japan

signals.name: HyperFix
signals.description: HyperFix was a radio-navigation system developed by Racal. Was used by vessels and ships. Has largely been phased out in favor of Differential GPS.

signals.name: Hyundai Mobis RKE-4F16 Key Fob
signals.description: Hyundai Mobis RKE-4F16 Wireless Key Fob for Hyundai Sonata models 2014-Present.

signals.name: ICAO Selcal
signals.description: ICAO Selcal (also known as AVCALL, ANNEX 10, or just SELCAL) is a HF/VHF aviation selective calling system used by ground stations to initiate radio communications with aircraft.

signals.name: ICARUS (International Cooperation for Animal Research Using Space)
signals.description: ICARUS aims its services primarily at scientific groups that perform basic and application-oriented research with migrating animals.

signals.name: ICV
signals.description: ICV is a NATO-operated VLF transmitted located in the island of Tavolara, Sardinia, Italy.

signals.name: ILS Marker Beacon
signals.description: ILS Marker Beacons are used by aircraft for Instrument Landing Systems, transmitted by an upward-facing directive antenna at known distances along the approach path.

signals.description: Radiosonde launched on a weather balloon.

signals.name: Improved Automatic Link Set-up (ALIS-2)
signals.description: ALIS-2, also known as RS-ARQ, RS ARQ 240, and MERLIN, is an improvement of the original ALIS system. ALIS-2 is used in the Rohde & Schwarz MERLIN modem.

signals.name: Industrial key opener
signals.description: key opener commonly used in industrial applications

signals.name: Inmarsat Aero
signals.description: Inmarsat Aero is the protocol that's used to link ground stations with aircraft via Inmarsat's satellite link. This protocol carries digital voice, fax and low speed data such as ACARS and ADS-C.

signals.name: Inmarsat Aero / L-band
signals.description: Inmarsat L-band satellite services near 1.5 GHz.

signals.name: Inmarsat IsatM2M
signals.description: IsatM2M Service operated by Inmarsat on existing Inmarsat-D/D+ infrastructure.

signals.description: Inmarsat C provides two-way data and messaging communication services to and from virtually anywhere in the world. The low-cost terminals and antennas are small enough to be fitted to any size of ship.

signals.name: Inmarsat-D(D+) Downlink
signals.description: Inmarsat D+ (and it's predecessor, Inmarsat D) was Inmarsat's satellite paging system. The main use of the technology was in tracking trucks and buoys and SCADA applications.

signals.name: Instrument Landing System
signals.description: Radio navigation system that allows aircraft to perform precision approaches in low visibility conditions.

signals.name: Integrated Digital Enhanced Network (iDEN)
signals.description: iDEN is a TDMA-based digital wireless standard developed by Motorola. It is a type of trunked radio with cellular phone benefits.

signals.description: ISDB-T (Integrated Services Digital Broadcasting – Terrestrial) is a new type of digital broadcasting system for providing audio, video and multimedia services. signals.name: Interoperable Electronic Train Management System (I-ETMS)
signals.description: Transmits train telemetry

signals.name: Ionized Meteor Trails
signals.description: Meteors traversing the E region of the atmosphere approximately 60 - 90 miles up create ionizing trails which can reflect and refract radio waves from commercial FM radio stations that are hundreds and sometimes thousands of miles away from the receiver.

signals.name: Ionosonde
signals.description: An Ionosonde (Also known as a chirpsounder or ionospheric sounder) is a radar that examines the Ionosphere and monitors HF propagation conditions by sweeping the HF band and receiving the echoes.

signals.name: IRA-ARQ
signals.description: IRA-ARQ, also known as BULG-ASCII and ASCII-ARQ, is a high data rate ARQ FSK system used by Bulgarian, Slovakian, and Czech diplomatic stations. The maximum speed of this mode has been seen to reach 1200 bd. Not seen much much nowadays

signals.name: Iranian 'Bubble' Jammer
signals.description: Iranian broadcast jammer with characteristic sound. Used to suppress Radio Farda and other independent stations which broadcast to Iranian audience.

signals.name: Iranian Navy QPSK Modem
signals.description: Iranian Navy QPSK Modem is a QPSK mode used by the Iranian Navy. It has gone through several versions. The current version (2015) is V2 and supports speeds of 468 Bd, 936 Bd, and 1872 Bd.

signals.name: Iridium
signals.description: This is the L-band uplink/downlink for the Low Earth Orbit Iridium Satellite Constellation. This system is used for satellite based phone calls.

signals.name: IS-54 D-AMPS
signals.description: D-AMPS, also known as IS-54 and IS-136, is a second generation (2G) mobile phone system standard which develops on analog AMPS, a 1G standard. This system is also colloquially known as TDMA.

signals.name: IsatData Pro
signals.description: Inmarsat's M2M data service for SCADA asset tracking and reporting.

signals.name: ISCAT
signals.description: Ionospheric Scattering (ISCAT) mode used for weak signal long distance radio contact by meteor and Ionosphere scattering.

signals.name: ISM 433 MHz Telemetry
signals.description: Short-range devices, keyfobs, sensors around 433.92 MHz.

signals.name: ISM 915 MHz
signals.description: US ISM band devices, telemetry, and IoT.

signals.name: ISM Band device
signals.description: An ISM band device such as a power meter or a wireless doorbell.

signals.name: ISM Band Weather sensor
signals.description: Data returned from a consumer weather sensor using the AlectoV1 protocol.

signals.name: Israeli Intelligence VFT
signals.description: Israeli Intelligence based FSK VFT.

signals.name: Israeli Navy Hybrid Modem (188-110 MOD)
signals.description: The Israeli Naval Hybrid Modem is based on the MIL-STD-188-110 Serial Standard. Has characteristic preamble with 4/6 Tone and 18 QPSK parallel mode before 110 Serial transmission. Possible use as a broadcast transmitter for ships. Used by the Israeli Navy 4XZ station from Haifa.

signals.name: Israeli VFT
signals.description: Israeli based VFT transmission, most likely used by Israeli government or military.

signals.name: Japan Military 8-Channel FSK
signals.description: Data signal thought to originate from Japanese Military/Navy

signals.name: Japanese Slot Machine (XSL)
signals.description: The Japanese Slot Machine (Enigma Designation XSL) is a simplex system used by the Japanese Maritime Self-Defense Force in Ichihara, Japan.

signals.name: Jim Creek (NLK)
signals.description: Jim Creek Naval Radio Station is used by the US Navy to transmit commands to distant submarines.

signals.name: Jindalee Operational Radar Network (JORN)
signals.description: JORN is an Australian OTHR system that operates uniquely in that it's radar bursts include an intro tone before the burst.

signals.name: JJY
signals.description: JJY, also known as JJY-40 and JJY-60, is the call sign for a pair of longwave Time Signal stations in Japan.

signals.name: John Deere RTK Radio 450
signals.description: Real-time Kinematic GPS is a satellite navigation technique used to enhance the precision of position data derived from satellite-based positioning systems (global navigation satellite systems, GNSS) such as GPS, BeiDou, GLONASS, Galileo and NavIC.

signals.name: JS8
signals.description: JS8Call is an extremely-weak-signal amateur radio communication mode based on FT8. It allows FT8 to be used for conversations and message relaying.

signals.name: JT65
signals.description: JT65 is an amateur radio QSO communication protocol developed by [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Hooton_Taylor_Jr Joe Taylor, K1JT]. JT65 has 3 submodes: JT65A, JT65B, and JT65C. The most popular submode of JT65 is JT65A. JT65 gets '65' from the 65 tones it uses.

signals.name: JT6M
signals.description: JT6M is part of the WSJT suite of digital weak signal software applications developed by Joe Taylor, K1JT

signals.name: JT9
signals.description: JT9 is a 9-FSK mode for making contact (QSO's) under extreme weak-signal conditions. It is part of the WSJT-X software.

signals.name: JTMS
signals.description: JTMS is a meteor scatter mode that uses MSK. JTMS behaves similarily to FSK441.

signals.name: Kenwood FleetSync
signals.description: FleetSync is a manufacturer specific signaling standard which includes a number of features: unit ID, status, emergency button, inhibit, status check, GPS, and selective calling.

signals.name: KG-STV
signals.description: KG-STV is an image transmission mode developed by JJ0OBZ in Japan.

signals.name: Kiwi
signals.description: Kiwi is a telemetry mode developed by CNES used on amateur rockets and radio balloons in France.

signals.name: KY57/58 voice encryption
signals.description: The KY57/58/68 Transmission Security Device is designed to protect the transmission of voice or data in the form of audio tones. Uses CVSD modulation like Securenet.

signals.name: Land Rover Discovery 4 Car Key
signals.description: 2FSK transmission mode 20828 baud, Information is transmitted by the code "Manchester", respectively, the data transfer rate is twice lower (7785.63 baud).

signals.name: Lentus
signals.description: Lentus is an extremely slow QRP mode developed by Patrick Lindecker F6CTE used to transmit QRP's at very low power. Each 43-character (75 bit) transmission takes roughly 5 minutes to transmit across 32 possible tones in a tight 25 Hz bandwidth.

signals.name: LEOSAR Downlink
signals.description: Cospas-Sarsat downlink from polar-orbiting weather satellites. The International Cospas-Sarsat Programme is a satellite-aided search and rescue initiative.

signals.name: Lightning Sferics
signals.description: VLF RF emissions from lightning in the atmosphere that can affect up to HF frequencies and beyond depending on strength. Has a popping crackle sound with both USB and AM modes of reception.

signals.name: Link-11
signals.description: Link-11 (Also known as ALLIGATOR, STANAG 5511, TADIL-A, MIL-STD-6011, and MIL-STD-188-203-1A) is a Tactical Data Link standard (formerly known as Tactical Digital Information Link (TADIL) used by NATO and the US Military for Maritime Tactical Data Exchange.

signals.name: Link-11 (UHF)
signals.description: This is the UHF band variant of Link-11, which is transmitted on a FM carrier. The FM-demodulated baseband is identical to the HF Link-11 waveform.

signals.name: Lockheed Martin LMS-6 (Radiosonde)
signals.description: The LMS-6 is a radiosonde developed by Lockheed Martin which contains a temperature, barometric pressure (On the 1680 MHz models only), and humidity sensor for upper air weather observations.

signals.name: Logic Trunked Radio (LTR)
signals.description: Logic Trunked Radio, is an analog trunked radio format developed by EF Johnson Company.

signals.name: Logitech(R) Wireless Mouse+Keyboard Signal
signals.description: This signal comes from Logitech(R) Brand wireless mouse and keyboard combo unit.

signals.name: LoJack
signals.description: LoJack is a vehicle tracking system that allows vehicles to be tracked by police, with the aim of recovering them in case of theft via a small radio transceiver clandestinely installed in a vehicle.

signals.name: LoRa
signals.description: LoRa (Long Range) is a proprietary low-power wide-area network modulation technique.

signals.name: LORAN
signals.description: LORAN (short for LOng RAnge Navigation) is a hyperbolic radio navigation system.

signals.name: Low Frequency Bicycle Computer Sensor
signals.description: This is an electromagnetic emission from a budget wireless bicycle computer speed sensor. signals.name: Low Rate Picture Transmission (LRPT)
signals.description: The Low Rate Picture Transmission (LRPT) is a digital transmission system, commonly transmitted by METEOR-M satellites, used to deliver weather images and data.

signals.name: LRS restaurant pager
signals.description: LRS restaurant pagers operate in the PMR446 band, most commonly on 446.15625 MHz. The system uses narrowband FM (NFM) modulation with a 12.5 kHz channel bandwidth, transmitting short data bursts that activate individual pagers.

signals.name: LTE / 4G
signals.description: 4G OFDM cellular carriers.

signals.name: LTE420 MCX
signals.description: Band 88 FDD

signals.description: An open source digital mode developed for amateur and other radio applications.

signals.name: M20 Radiosonde
signals.description: Telemetry signal transmitted by M20 radiosondes

signals.name: Magnetron (microwave owen)
signals.description: Magnetron produces regularly repeating pulses of microwave energy. These pulses have a defined repetition rate, a stable peak amplitude, and a consistent pulse width.

signals.name: Marconi Selenia 25-Tone Modem
signals.description: The Marconi Selenia 25-Tone Modem is a military modem developed sometime around 2003 by Marconi Selenia Communications (Now Finmeccanica). It supports ECCM capability and transmits at a datarate of 2400bps. This mode was employed by Turkey.

signals.name: Marine VHF
signals.description: International maritime mobile FM voice channels.

signals.name: Mazda SKE126-01 Key Fob
signals.description: SKE126-01 Key Fob used for multiple Mazda models between 2006-2014. Manufactured by Mitsubishi Electric Company.

signals.name: Mazielka (X06)
signals.description: Mazielka (X06) is a diplomatic selcall system used by the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Used to alert that a Serdolik transmission is going to occur soon, usually on a different frequency.

signals.name: MD-522
signals.description: MD-522 (Also known as MIL-M-55529A) is a synchronous FSK mode built into GRC-MD522 teletypewriter sets and used for wirelessly transmitting ASCII information. MD-522 has a narrowband, wideband, and diversity mode.

signals.name: MD-674
signals.description: MD-674, also known as Wireline FSK, is a very old United States Military FSK Modem from the 1960's. Uses 85 Hz FSK shift. Speeds of 50 Bd, 75 Bd, 100 Bd, and 150 Bd have been logged. No longer seen today.

signals.name: MDC-4800
signals.description: Motorola's MDC-4800 is a data protocol that was used in ARDIS and DataTAC Networks as well as in MDT networks. RD-LAP was derived from this mode. Also known as Motorola Mobile Data Communications System (MODACOM)

signals.name: MDC1200
signals.description: MDC (Motorola Data Communications), also known as Stat-Alert, MDC-1200 and MDC-600, is a Motorola two-way radio low-speed data system.

signals.name: Meteomodem M10 Weather Balloon (Radiosonde)
signals.description: Weather balloon (radiosonde) telemetry data.

signals.name: Meteomodem PilotSonde Weather Balloon
signals.description: Weather balloon telemetry data.

signals.name: METEOR-M High Resolution Picture Transmission (HRPT)
signals.description: A variant of the [[High_Resolution_Picture_Transmission_(HRPT)|NOAA HRPT]] signal, which has a different data structure and better low-signal handling characteristics.

signals.name: Meteor-M LRPT
signals.description: Russian Meteor-M low-rate picture transmission.

signals.name: Meteosat WEFAX
signals.description: Meteosat WEFAX is a WEFAX used to transmit satellite images via Meteosat Satellites. WEFAX was introduced with the first Meteosat in 1977.

signals.name: METOP Advanced High Resolution Picture Transmission (AHRPT)
signals.description: A high-speed digital link used by METOP weather satellites for direct data dissemination.

signals.name: MFJ-269C Antenna SWR Analyzer
signals.description: Popular antenna analyzer among ham operators and the like. Output power is only ~20mW so if heard, source is nearby. Other MFJ models may be similar.

signals.name: Microsonde Mark II Weather Balloon - LORAN-C signal (Radiosonde)
signals.description: Weather balloon telemetry data. The LORAN-C signal is mixed into the carrier.

signals.name: Microwave motion sensor (doppler radar module)
signals.description: Microwave motion sensor uses a small Doppler radar module to detect movement. The sensor emits microwave signals and monitors the reflected waves.

signals.name: MIL-STD-110-342
signals.description: MIL-STD-110-342 was a US Dept. of Defense standard for a 16 channel VFT teletype transmission. This mode was officially cancelled as of December 5th, 1995.

signals.name: MIL-STD-188-110 Appendix A 16-Tone
signals.description: MIL-STD-188-110 Appendix A is a 16-tone OFDM PSK signal used to transmit data. As of 110C revision, this mode is being phased out.

signals.name: MIL-STD-188-110 Appendix B 39-Tone
signals.description: MIL-STD-188-110 Appendix B is a 39-tone OFDM DQPSK mode used to send data and voice.

signals.name: MIL-STD-188-110 Serial
signals.description: MIL-STD-188-110 Serial is a US Department of Defense standard for HF Communications, Serial PSK mode. Can transmit both data and voice with a range of interleaving and speed modes for optimal propagation.

signals.name: Military UHF Airband
signals.description: Military AM airband voice, 225–400 MHz.

signals.name: Milstar
signals.description: UHF FHSS Downlink of Milstar, a US joint military service satellite communications system that provides secure, jam resistant, worldwide communications. Nicknamed 'Waterdroplets' for it's characteristic waveform and sound.

signals.name: MMP-4800
signals.description: MMP-4800 was a MDT (Mobile Data Terminal) protocol developed by Canadian company Mobile Data International (MDI) in 1982 for their Mobile Data Terminals. Used by public safety and commercial industries. Phased out.

signals.name: MOBITEX
signals.description: MOBITEX is an OSI based open standard, national public access wireless packet-switched data network.

signals.name: MODAT
signals.description: MODAT is a 7-tone Automatic Number Identification (ANI) status system used by handheld radios. It provides unit ID and emergency statuses to receiving radio sets when transmitted.

signals.name: Modernised High Frequency Communications System (MHFCS)
signals.description: The Modernised High Frequency Communications System (MHFCS) is an Australian Department of Defense HF System for their military communications network. Also known as AUS MIL ISB Modem, AUS MHFCS, and ADF HFCS.

signals.name: Monaco Enterprises MAAP Fire Alarm
signals.description: Fire alarm control panel built for the United States of America's Department of Defense.

signals.name: MONITOR-2(RS39S)
signals.description: Monitor-2 is a Russian 3u Cubesat used for cosmic flare observation. It is most likely only active when above Russia.

signals.name: Morse Code (CW)
signals.description: CW Morse Code is the simplest form of transmission found virtually all over the RF bands for a variety of uses. The most common use of this is for Call-sign Beacons by both Amateur and Military operators.

signals.name: Motorola ASTRO 25 HPD Air Interface
signals.description: Motorola's ASTRO 25 High Performance Data Air Interface allows Motorola ASTRO 25 HPD modems to transfer data at up to 96 kbps over a 25 kHz channel in the 700 MHz or 800 MHz bands.

signals.name: Motorola MOSCAD SCADA telemetry
signals.description: Motorola MOSCAD, is motorola's FSK version of SCADA for Data acquisition.

signals.name: Motorola SECURENET
signals.description: Motorola SECURENET ("analog" encryption) was a secure voice option for conventional and Motorola Type II trunked systems, encoding the voice using 12kbps CVSD and encrypting the bitstream. signals.name: Motorola Type II
signals.description: Radio trunking control channel.

signals.description: Motorola DMR-based commercial digital radio.
