signals.name: MPT 1327
signals.description: MPT1327 (Ministry of Posts and Telegraph 1327) is a signaling protocol standard for analog trunked radio

signals.name: MPT1394 Keyfob
signals.description: Remote key less entry fob for Honda car's with door lock, Unlock and remote boot/trunk open feature (keyfob data may be same as other manufactures)

signals.name: MRZ-3MK Weather Balloon (radiosonde)
signals.description: MRZ-3MK is a Russian weather radiosonde.

signals.name: MRZ-N1 Weather Balloon (radiosonde)
signals.description: MRZ-N1 is a russian weather radiosonde.

signals.name: MSF
signals.description: MSF is a time signal station in Anthorn, United Kingdom, which broadcasts the UK national time reference

signals.name: MSK144
signals.description: MSK144 is a Minimum Shift Keying FSK signal used for amateur radio meteor-scatter contacts. It transmits 144 bit long packets at a baudrate of 2000 bps using frequencies 1000 and 2000 Hz.

signals.name: MSM-1250 Modem
signals.description: MSM-1250 (Medium Speed Modem) is a 10 FSK-2 OFDM digital data protocol used by the stand-alone modem "SkyFax", used to transmit and receive faxes on HF.

signals.name: MT63
signals.description: MT63 is a Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexed (OFDM) digital data mode aimed for use in high noise environments.

signals.name: Multi Frequency Shift Keying (MFSK)
signals.description: MFSK is a generic family of frequency shift keying digital transmission methods using more than the two tones of BFSK (binary FSK). Many digital signals, especially on HF, use MFSK including WSPR, FT4 and FT8. MFSK-8 and MFSK-16 are two other well-known amateur radio modes.

signals.name: Multiple sub-Nyquist Sampling Encoding (MUSE)
signals.description: Multiplite sub-Nyquist Sampling Encoding (MUSE) also known as Hi-Vision was a early analogue high-defition television standard developed by NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories. Replaced by digital ISDB broadcast since 2007.

signals.name: Multiplexed Analogue Components (MAC)
signals.description: Multiplexed Analogue Components (MAC/packet) family was a analogue television broadcasting standard. Replaced by digital broadcast.

signals.name: Multitone Paging
signals.description: Multitone Paging signal, developed by Multitone Electronics in the UK. Uses similar coding to POCSAG but the headers are different and only work with Multitone's range of paging products

signals.name: Narrow-Bandwidth Television (NBTV)
signals.description: Narrow-Bandwidth Television (NBTV).

signals.name: NATEL
signals.description: NATEL is a 5-tone selcall mode defined by Scandinavian National Telephone recommendations.

signals.name: NAVTEX
signals.description: Maritime safety text broadcasts using SITOR-B FSK.

signals.name: NB-IOT
signals.description: Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) is a Low Power Wide Area Network (LPWAN) radio technology standard developed by 3GPP to enable a wide range of cellular devices and services.

signals.name: Near Field Communication (NFC)
signals.description: Near-field communication (NFC) is a set of communication protocols that enables communication between two electronic devices over a distance of 4 cm (11⁄2 in) or less.

signals.name: Near Instantaneous Companded Audio Multiplex (NICAM)
signals.description: NICAM is used to provide digital stereo audio alongside PAL video for television broadcasts.

signals.name: Next Generation Digital Narrowband (NXDN)
signals.description: NXDN is a digital narrowband trunked radio protocol used in commercial, business & industry, transport and Public Safety professional radio systems.

signals.name: NFM Voice
signals.description: Used in analog walkie-talkies and communication systems.

signals.name: Nissan Car Key
signals.description: Wireless entry rolling code car key.

signals.name: Nissan Qashqai Keyless Entry LF (Intelligent Key)
signals.description: This signal is the Low Frequency (LF) interrogation ping from a Nissan Qashqai (Intelligent Key / Keyless Entry system). The vehicle's Body Control Module (BCM) transmits short 125 kHz ASK-modulated pulses via internal and external antennas to detect the presence of the key fob.

signals.name: NML
signals.description: Naval Radio Transmitter Facility (NRTF) transmits encrypted commands to submerged US submarines.

signals.name: NOAA APT
signals.description: NOAA weather satellite Automatic Picture Transmission.

signals.name: NOAA Direct Sounder Broadcast (DSB)
signals.description: The Direct Sounder Broadcast (DSB) is an auxiliary telemetry downlink from NOAA Polar Operational Environmental Satellites (POES), transmitted alongside Automatic Picture Transmission (APT) broadcasts.

signals.name: NOAA ITOS High Resolution Picture Transmission (HRPT)
signals.description: An analog signal broadcast from NOAA ITOS polar satellites that transmitted images from the VHRR radiometer.

signals.name: NOAA POES High Resolution Picture Transmission (HRPT)
signals.description: A digital link to transmit images and other data collected from the satellite at a high resolution.

signals.name: NOAA Weather Radio
signals.description: US continuous weather broadcasts on seven VHF channels.

signals.name: Nokia Adaptive Message Terminal
signals.description: The Nokia Adaptive Message Terminal, also known as Nokia Adaptive Burst Modem and Kryapp 302, is a Finnish encrypted messaging system suggested to be used by Finnish Intelligence Services and Swedish Military.

signals.name: Non-Directional Beacon (NDB)
signals.description: A Non-Directional Beacon (NDB) is a ground-based, low frequency radio transmitter used as an instrument approach for airports and offshore platforms.

signals.name: North Korean Diplo FSK
signals.description: North Korean Diplomatic FSK link, teletype radio diplomatic usage. Also known as DPRK-FSK, KRE-FSK, DPRK-ARQ, and KEGURI. Has a FEC stream mode and a burst ARQ mode.

signals.name: North Korean Diplo PSK
signals.description: North Korean Diplomatic PSK link. Also known as KRE-PSK. Four speed modes have been seen, 150 bd, 300 bd, 600 bd, and 1200 bd. All use BPSK modulation. The main identifying feature of this signal are the preambles and end of transmission patterns.

signals.name: North Korean noise jammer
signals.description: Noise jammer with a carrier than tends to switch frequencies slightly lower and higher than the main signal frequency. Commonly found on 6.6 MHz

signals.name: North Korean Siren Jammer
signals.description: The North Korean Siren Jammer is among the signal disruption techniques employed by North Korea, commonly targeting shortwave radio stations.

signals.name: NOV
signals.description: TACAMO (take charge and move out) is the back up communications system to the US nuclear submarine fleet in case an attack on land based transmitters disables them. signals.name: NPM
signals.description: Naval Radio Transmitting Facility (NRTF) sends encrypted commands to submerged US naval submarines in the Pacific.

signals.name: NTSC Broadcast
signals.description: National Television System Committee (NTSC) Television broadcast is an analogue television broadcast mode. Currently being phased out in parts of the world in favor of digital broadcast.

signals.name: NWC
signals.description: Naval Communication Station (NCS) Harold E. Holt. Used jointly by the Australian and United States navies to transmit encrypted orders to submerged submarines in the Pacific.

signals.name: OFDM NBTV
signals.description: OFDM NBTV is an analog technique, in fact it is a true Fuzzy design as well. The transmission technique used is quite different from conventional TV

signals.name: Olivia
signals.description: OLIVIA is an amateur digital teletype mode designed by Pawel Jalocha SP9VRC in 2005. Its goal was to be effective even in poor propagation conditions.

signals.name: One Beep, Two Beeps
signals.description: One Beep, Two Beeps is a nickname given to a signal emitted by the Norwegian Navy communications center in Bodø

signals.name: OOK RC Car Remote Control
signals.description: Cheap RC Cars with only for buttons (Forward, Reverse, Left, Right) Typically use 27Mhz or 49Mhz as the transmit frequency. There's typically no channel switching system on the remote control, which leads to interference with operating two RC vehicles at once.

signals.name: OpenSky
signals.description: OpenSky is an encrypted TDMA protocol that is heavily used but is being phased out by the Pennsylvania State Police. No one other than the intended user has been able to decrypt the signal.

signals.name: OpenWay CENTRON Smart-Meter
signals.description: This is a signal from a OpenWay Centron Electric 'Smart Meter'. Each house is now fitted with one of these, and they are strong - typically 50 dB above the atmospheric noise level.

signals.name: OPERA Beacon and Data
signals.description: OPERA Ad-Hoc Data/Beacon. The system is unique in that utilizes a serial data stream and Manchester coding, its therefore impossible to lose lock and its extremely robust in disturbed paths and heavy static.

signals.name: Orbcomm
signals.description: Orbcomm satellites are used for monitoring and sending short text messages.

signals.name: OrbComm Mobile Telephony
signals.description: Orbcomm digitized mobile satellite-based telephone signal intercepted over Hawaii, preceding NOAA 19 pass.

signals.name: OTP-2 Satellite Musical Beacon
signals.description: Musical transmission originating from the OTP-2 Cubesat

signals.name: P03 numbers station
signals.description: Enigma designation P03 is a family of digital PSK modes, used by the "Polish 11" numbers station operator, which is likely a Polish intelligence agency.

signals.name: P07 numbers station
signals.description: Enigma designation P07 is a custom digital mode used by the "Russian 7" numbers station operator which is likely a major Russian intelligence agency.

signals.name: PACKET
signals.description: Packet, also known as FSK300, AFSK1200, BPSK300, QPSK600, BPSK1200, QPSK2400, AX.25 and IL2P, is a packet based protocol derived from X.25 and HDLC computer network protocols. Packet radio is a synchronous system in which data is transmitted in frames.

signals.name: PACTOR I
signals.description: PACTOR-I is a digital data protocol combining elements of PACKET and AMTOR ARQ.

signals.name: PACTOR II
signals.description: PACTOR II is an advancement of PACTOR I. It is up to 8 times faster than PACTOR I.

signals.name: PACTOR III
signals.description: PACTOR III introduces 6 speed levels that provide higher throughput and improved robustness compared to PACTOR I and II. PACTOR III is on average 3.5 times faster than PACTOR II. With optimal conditions, PACTOR III becomes over 5 times faster.

signals.name: PACTOR IV
signals.description: PACTOR IV is the newest iteration of the PACTOR series, advancing from PACTOR I-III. It is 1.5x-3x faster than PACTOR III, and has 10 speed levels.

signals.name: Pager (POCSAG 1200)
signals.description: [POCSAG 1200] Used in places like hospitals and other areas. Transmits at 1200 bps.

signals.name: PAL Broadcast
signals.description: Phase Alternating Line (PAL) Analogue Television Broadcast. Now phased out in most of the world.

signals.name: Panther-H Modem
signals.description: Panther-H is an intelligent frequency hopping transceiver developed by Racal (now Thales Group). Has a signature 8-burst SOC (Start Of Conversation) sync procedure. Used in Panther-2000H radios

signals.name: PAX
signals.description: PAX and PAX2 are developed by Patrick Lindecker F6CTE in 2005, and was derived from Olivia. It utilizes the AX.25 protocol that PACKET uses, and had a minimum SNR of -10dB. Can transmit APRS frames.

signals.name: Phase Shift Keying (PSK)
signals.description: PSK is a digital teletype mode based on Phase-Shift Keying (PSK) modulation. The most popular amateur radio PSK mode is PSK 31.

signals.name: PI4
signals.description: PI4 (PharusIgnis4) is a 4-MFSK mode designed for amateur radio beacons. It is designed to work via different propagation modes.

signals.name: Piccolo
signals.description: Piccolo was a MFSK system developed by the UK Foreign and Commonwealth Office (FCO) to communicate with foreign embassies and UK military stations around the world. No longer used.

signals.name: PLUTO II OTH Radar
signals.description: PLUTO II is an Over The Horizon Radar located in the Sovereign Base Area just outside RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus. PLUTO II is very active in Europe.

signals.name: PMR446
signals.description: European license-free UHF handheld FM.

signals.name: POCSAG
signals.description: POCSAG (Post Office Code Standardisation Advisory Group), also known as Super-POCSAG, Radio Paging Code No. 1 or RPC1, is a one-way 2FSK paging protocol that supports 512, 1200, and 2400 bps.

signals.name: Podsolnukh 'Sunflower' Radar
signals.description: A Russian over the horizon radar, also known as "Sunflower"

signals.name: POL-ARQ
signals.description: POL-ARQ was a duplex ARQ system used by Polish and Italian diplomatic services. This system uses the CCIR 476-4 alphabet with polatiry retained. No longer in use.

signals.name: Polish Intelligence 100bd 625Hz FSK
signals.description: Also known as F11, this is a one-way broadcast system that was used by one of Polish intelligence agencies for delivery of messages to their operatives abroad on fixed schedules.

signals.name: Portable Traffic Lights
signals.description: Signals sent from portable traffic lights that are often used at roadworks.

signals.name: Positive Train Control (PTC)
signals.description: Positive train control (PTC) is a system of functional requirements for monitoring and controlling train movements as an attempt to provide increased safety.

signals.name: PRC-16
signals.description: PRC-16 is a Chinese sourced PSK data link, traced to Shanghai. Suspected user Chinese Military.

signals.name: Primary Aeronautical Surveillance Radar
signals.description: A Primary radar (PSR Primary Surveillance Radar) is a conventional radar sensor that illuminates a large portion of space with an electromagnetic wave and receives back the reflected waves from targets within that space.

signals.name: Primex Wireless Time Sync
signals.description: Primex Wireless Time Sync is a VHF Time Synchronization signal used in Primex Wireless's XR Series.

signals.name: PROBA 1/2 Downlink
signals.description: Dump of satellite data to Redu, Belgium ground station from the PROBA (Project for On-Board Autonomy) 1, 2, and V ESA satellites.

signals.name: Project 25 (P25)
signals.description: Project 25 (P25 or APCO-25) is a trunked radio standard developed by The Association of Public Safety Communications Officials International (APCO-25) for use with public safety organizations around the world.

signals.name: ProVoice
signals.description: ProVoice is a digital voice mode used in EDACS trunked systems.

signals.name: PSK Paging link
signals.description: Also known as PSK paging, is a signal that allows side-by-side PSK to exist in AFSK paging links, allowing for more dynamically processed DSP available.

signals.name: PSK-AM
signals.description: PSK-AM is an amateur digital mode developed by Patrick Lindecker F6CTE in 2002/2003, and incorporates FEC interleaving. PSK-AM uses the modulation of PSK10/31 with the FEC of SITOR-B.

signals.name: PSK2K
signals.description: PSK2K is a meteor scatter type of mode written by DJ5HG Using a modulation scheme of BPSK at 2000 Bd.

signals.name: Pulse Coded Modulated (PCM) RC Toy
signals.description: Signal used for remote control (RC) Toys.

signals.name: Pursuit Wireless Car Key
signals.description: Pursuit series wireless car alarm entry key, for use on vehicles equipped with Pursuit Series Car Alarm System.

signals.name: Q-MAC HF Modem
signals.description: The Q-MAC HF Modem is a military modem developed by Q-MAC (acquired by Barrett Communications). It uses OFDM with a BPSK sync channel in a gap of the signal.

signals.name: Q15X25
signals.description: Q15X25, also known as NEWQPSK, is an experimental amateur radio packet modem developed by Pawel Jalocha SP9VRC. Q15X25 is a OFDM QPSK implementation of the AX.25 Packet protocol used in PACKET.

signals.name: Q65
signals.description: Q65 is a 65-FSK extreme weak-signal mode which is designed for Earth-Moon-Earth communications and fast-fading propagation modes such as tropospheric scatter, rain scatter and trans-equatorial propagation. It offers a variety of submodes. Q65 is part of the WSJT-X software.

signals.name: QO-100-modem
signals.description: High speed modem for QO-100 (Es'hail 2) amateur satellite narrow transponder.

signals.name: Quadcopter Telemetry Signal
signals.description: This signal originates from the Silicon Instruments Si1000 Software Defined Radio (SDR) that is a component of the 3DR Telemetry Radio, sold for use as a data link between a computer ground station and a UAV "a drone".

signals.name: Quansheng UVK5 Digital Text Message
signals.description: A digital text message protocol included in the stock firmware of some Quansheng brand handheld radios to send up to 30 characters in a short packet type message.

signals.name: RAC-ARQ
signals.description: RAC-ARQ, also known as MEROD and RACAL-ARQ, is a teleprinter system by Racal, used in MEROD devices. MEROD stands for Message Entry and Read Out Device. Hasn't been seen since 2010.

signals.name: Radar altimeter
signals.description: Aircrafts radar altimeter.

signals.name: Radio Data Link Access Procedure (RD-LAP)
signals.description: Motorola's Radio Data Link Access Procedure (RD-LAP) is a 1G protocol that was used in ARDIS and DataTAC Networks, and is still used in some MDT's, as well as gas companies, police departments, fire departments, financial companies, etc.

signals.name: Radio Data System (RDS)
signals.description: Radio Data System (RDS) and its North American variant, Radio Broadcast Data System (RBDS), are data modes transmitted on subcarriers of commercial FM radio station transmissions.

signals.name: Radio Navigation Satellite System (RNSS)
signals.description: Generic positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) signals transmitted by global/regional navigation satellite system (GNSS/RNSS) and Satellite-Based Augmentation System (SBAS) constellations such as GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, QZSS, and IRNSS.

signals.name: Radio Telephone Network C (C-Netz)
signals.description: The Radio Telephone Network C (German: Funktelefonnetz-C, abbreviated as C-Netz), was a first generation analog cellular phone system deployed and operated in Germany (at first West Germany) by DeTeMobil (formerly of Deutsche Bundespost Telekom, currently Deutsche Telekom).

signals.name: Radio Teletype (RTTY)
signals.description: RTTY (Also known as Baudot or ITA2) uses the Baudot 5-bit alphabet with FSK to send text messages over the shortwave. This mode is gradually dying out in favor of more robust modes like PSK31 in the amateur service.

signals.name: Radio-relay link
signals.description: A radio‑relay (microwave) link using small parabolic antennas is a short‑range, high‑capacity point‑to‑point microwave connection commonly deployed when fiber is unavailable or too expensive to build.

signals.name: Radioteknicheskaya Systema Dalney Navigatsii (RSDN-20)
signals.description: RSDN-20, also known as Alpha, is a Russian hyperbolic radio navigation system. Presumed to be used for Russian ships, submarines and aircraft in the northern hemisphere, possibly worldwide.

signals.name: Railroad VHF
signals.description: North American railroad AAR VHF FM channels.

signals.name: Rain Master sprinkler control
signals.description: Control signal for grass sprinkler watering system

signals.name: RBU
signals.description: RBU is a time code radio station located in Moscow. It transmits a continuous 10 kW time code on 66.66 kHz.

signals.name: RDL VLF
signals.description: RDL is a Russian VLF station located in Krasnodar. It is one of the few VLF stations that changes modes during routine transmissions.

signals.name: Redundant Digital File Transfer (RDFT)
signals.description: RDFT is an amateur radio digital mode used to transmit files.

signals.name: ReFLEX
signals.description: ReFLEX is a two-way paging variant of FLEX.

signals.name: Relocatable Over-the-Horizon Radar (ROTHR)
signals.description: Relocatable Over-the-Horizon Radar (ROTHR), also known as AN/TPS-71, is an OTH Radar used by the United States Navy that uses bistatic ionospheric backscattering for wide area surveillance.

signals.name: RF heating and welding interference
signals.description: Radio frequency heating and welding equipment may radiate interference which can be picked up by radio receivers. On a waterfall display, it usually appears as wobbly peaks that rapidly drift downwards in frequency.

signals.name: RFID
signals.description: Radio-frequency identification (RFID) uses electromagnetic fields to automatically identify and track tags attached to objects. The tags contain electronically-stored information. Passive tags collect energy from a nearby RFID reader's interrogating radio waves.

signals.name: Road Coordination/Maintenance Telemetry
signals.description: A sort of SCADA signaling method used to cooordinate traffic or other road works using external NFM transmitters. Can also be shared with road commission vehicles and related things.

signals.name: Robust PACKET
signals.description: Robust PACKET, also known as HF-APRS, RPR, Winlink RMS, and APRSlink, is an OFDM version of the amateur mode PACKET which is optimized for shortwave use. This mode was developed by Spezielle Communications Systeme GmbH & Co. KG (SCS).

signals.name: ROS
signals.description: ROS is an amateur radio teletype free running QSO mode designed for low signal/high noise conditions.

signals.name: RTTYM
signals.description: RTTYM, developed by Nick Fedoseev (UT2UZ) in 2005, is a digital mode derived from Olivia. It aims to deliver a compromise of speed and performance. RTTYM is about 4x faster than Olivia, but trades the speed for reduced robustness and sensitivity.

signals.name: RUM-FEC
signals.description: RUM-FEC, also known as ROU-FEC and SAU-FEC, is a FSK FEC system used by Romanian diplomatic services. This is no longer used today, replaced by MIL-STD 188-110 Serial.

signals.name: RUM-MOI FEC
signals.description: RUM-MOI FEC, also known as RUM-MIL 115.76 Bd, is a FSK FEC mode used by the Romanian Ministry of Internal Affairs, supposedly under military use. This is no longer used today, replaced by MIL-STD 188-110 Serial.

signals.name: Russian Diplo VFT PSK 64Bd
signals.description: Russian Diplomatic 3 channel VFT PSK running at 64 Bd. Enigma M42 designation

signals.name: Russian Intelligence 200bd 1000Hz FSK (F06)
signals.description: Also known as F06, this is a one-way error-correcting broadcast system, used by one of Russian intelligence agencies for delivery of messages to their operatives abroad on fixed schedules.

signals.name: Russian Intelligence 200bd 500Hz FSK (F01)
signals.description: Also known as F01, this is a digital FSK mode used by Russian intelligence to deliver encrypted messages to their operatives abroad. Transmissions usually happen on fixed schedules.

signals.name: Russian MFSK-OFDM-chirp hybrid modem
signals.description: A supposedly Russian HF data mode with MFSK, OFDM and frequency sweeps, resulting in an interesting spectrogram and sound.

signals.name: Russian military 20bd 7kHz FSK
signals.description: Slow 20-baud FSK signal with very large 7 kHz frequency shift. Used by Russian military.

signals.name: Russian OTH 'Ghadir' type
signals.description: Over The Horizon radar with a very similar signal structure as Ghadir. Operating in west Russia.

signals.name: Russian overhead power line telemetry system
signals.description: Russian telemetry system, transmitted over the overhead power lines.

signals.name: RWM
signals.description: RWM is a Russian shortwave time signal station.

signals.name: S-Band Jammer
signals.description: This is what the signal of a military S-Band (In this case 2.4 GHz) RADAR and WiFi intentional interference (Jamming) device looks like. This signal is generated by a DDS system and is then used to modulate the output of a 2.45 GHz magnetron (The same as in a microwave oven).

signals.name: Saab Grintek MHF-50 MFSK Modem
signals.description: The MHF-50 MFSK Modem by Saab Grintek Technologies in South Africa is a data modem that utilizes RTTY, 2-FSK, and 33-MFSK to transmit data

signals.name: Samsung Washing Machine Interference
signals.description: Interference from a samsung washing machine. Manifests as lines and bulb-looking patterns across the spectrum.

signals.name: SAS/SRC
signals.description: Swedish navy transmitter for submarine communication. It shares the antenna with SAQ (Grimeton Radio)

signals.name: SAS2
signals.description: Swedish navy transmitter for submarine communication. It shares the antenna with SAQ (Grimeton Radio) and is activated less often as the other Swedish transmitters used for VLF submarine communication. Usually, it works with reduced power.

signals.name: SAS3
signals.description: Swedish navy transmitter for submarine communication. It shares the antenna with SAQ (Grimeton Radio).

signals.name: Schneider Trio E-Series Modem
signals.description: Schneider Trio E-Series Modems are industrial modems used for SCADA, telemetry, and other ASCII-based messaging applications.

signals.name: SECAM
signals.description: Sequential Colour with Memory (SECAM) Analogue Television Broadcast. Now phased out in most of the world.

signals.name: Secondary surveillance radar (SSR)
signals.description: Secondary surveillance radar (SSR)is a radar system used in air traffic control. A surveillance radar system which uses transmitters/receivers (interrogators) and transponders.

signals.name: SECOR 4 (EGRS 4)
signals.description: SECOR 4 (''COSPAR ID: 1965-027B'') was a SEquential COllation of Range series satellite, and is occasionally active when receiving adequate solar power on it's panels. It is not consistent, likely owing to a tumbling or rotating motion.

signals.name: SELCAL
signals.description: HF/VHF selective calling tones for aircraft.

signals.name: Sensus Water meter (Acquisition units)
signals.description: These are samples from the Sensus Water meters. They are a FHSS ASK encoded data transmission for purposes of providing municipalities water meter telemetry (for billing how much water you use).

signals.name: Serdolik
signals.description: Serdolik is a MFSK signal used by the Russian diplomatic service.

signals.name: Shortwave Broadcast
signals.description: International HF AM broadcast services.

signals.name: SHR
signals.description: Swedish navy transmitter for submarine communication. It shares the antenna with SAQ (Grimeton Radio).

signals.name: SI-ARQ
signals.description: SI-ARQ, also known as ARQ-S and ARQ-1000S, is a simplex ARQ system designed by Siemens formerly used by Austrian and Indonesian diplomatic services. No longer used today.

signals.name: SI-FEC
signals.description: SI-FEC, also known as FEC-S, FEC 1000 Simplex, and FEC-1000S, was the FEC variant of SI-ARQ, and was only used under extremely poor propagation conditions. SI-FEC was developed by Siemens and was used by Austrian and Indonesian diplomatic services.

signals.name: Siemens 1.5T MRI Scanner
signals.description: Radio signal used by MRI machines to excite protons and obtain their response.

signals.name: Siemens CHX-200 FSK Modem
signals.description: CHX200, also known as Siemens CHP200 and PRC-921/GY, is a backpack HF ECCOM transceiver, designed and built by Siemens.

signals.name: SIGFOX
signals.description: SIGFOX is a IoT wireless network system utilizing ETSI's specification for Low Throughput Networks (LTN) and Ultra Narrow-Band (UNB) modulation.

signals.name: SIMONe meteor radar
signals.description: The SIMONe radar is a meteor detection system that is operated in multiple research sites around the world. It uses continuous spread-spectrum coded transmissions which gives it an unusual sound when demodulated into audio. It can be received over long distances during sporadic-E

signals.name: Single frequency russian overhead power line telemetry system
signals.description: Russian telemetry system, transmitted over the overhead power lines.

signals.name: Single Sideband Voice
signals.description: Single-sideband voice is a subtype of AM voice modulation. It is used in HF amateur bands and for weak signal VHF and UHF voice, as well as aircraft weather reports.

signals.name: SiriusXM Satellite Radio
signals.description: SiriusXM Satellite Radio: Terrestrial Repeater Signal

signals.name: SITOR-A
signals.description: SITOR-A (Also known as AMTOR-A) is one of two modes of SITOR, which stands for Simplex Teletype Over Radio.

signals.name: SITOR-B
signals.description: SITOR-B is one of two modes of SITOR (Simplex Teletype Over Radio).

signals.name: SKiYMET meteor radar
signals.description: SKiYMET is a meteor detection radar which is used by many research institutes around the world. It can use different transmission parameters and can be received over long distances during sporadic-E and other special propagation conditions.

signals.name: SkyOFDM
signals.description: Data transmission mode developed by SkySweep Technologies in Finland. Probably used by Finnish MFA

signals.name: Slow-Scan Television (SSTV)
signals.description: Slow-scan television (SSTV) is a method for picture transmission used by amateur radio operators to transmit and receive images.

signals.name: Smart TV Interference
signals.description: Interference from Smart TV units

signals.name: Snap Circuits SCROV-10 Remote Control
signals.description: A remote control transmission from the controller from an Elenco Snap Circuits SCROV-10 kit.

signals.name: SNOTEL (Snow Telemetry)
signals.description: SNOTEL stations are a set of precipitation and other sensors spread across the mountains of the United States by the Department of Agriculture through the National Resources Conservation Service.

signals.name: SOLRAD 7B (COSPAR ID: 1965-016D)
signals.description: SOLRAD-7B is one of the many "zombie satellites" in orbit and is an artifact of the mid 1960's US space program. It occasionally will become active again when illuminated by sunlight due to the satellite bus having several small, semi-circular solar panels.

signals.name: Sonne
signals.description: Sonne (Called Consol by the Britons) was a low-frequency radio range based radio navigation system used for long range navigation.

signals.name: Soyuz-MS spacecraft telemetry
signals.description: Russian spacecraft telemetry system.

signals.name: SP-14 (XP)
signals.description: SP-14 (XP) was a 14 tone MFSK mode with origins from the Russian Intelligence and Foreign Ministry. Also known as NUM-13. Inactive since 2005, superseded by XPA.

signals.name: Spectrum Painting
signals.description: A form of SSTV that directly modulates an image to IQ by scanning across it so it shows up when viewed using a waterfall. Used by Hams for experimentation methods.

signals.name: SPREAD
signals.description: SPREAD, also known as AUTOSPEC Mk2, SPREAD-11, SPREAD-21, and SPREAD-51, was a FEC system used by Romanian diplomatic stations and the Brazilian Navy and shore stations. SPREAD is considered the successor to AUTOSPEC.

signals.name: STANAG 4197
signals.description: STANAG 4197 is a NATO QPSK OFDM signal used in ANDVT modems that transmit encrypted digital voice over HF.

signals.name: STANAG 4285
signals.description: STANAG 4285 is specified by the NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) Military Agency for Standardization in "Characteristics of 1200 / 2400 / 3600 Bits per Second Single Tone Modulators / Demodulators for HF Radio Links"

signals.name: STANAG 4415
signals.description: STANAG 4415 is a NATO standard for robust, non-hopping digital data communication, used on severely degraded HF channels with large Doppler and multipath spreads.

signals.name: STANAG 4481
signals.description: STANAG 4481, also known as CRATT, Link-4, and NATO-75, is specified by the NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) Military Agency for Standardization as a "Minimum technical equipment standards for naval HF shore-to-ship broadcast system"

signals.name: STANAG 4529
signals.description: STANAG 4529 a modification of STANAG 4285 to deliver data and voice in 1240 Hz of bandwidth at rates of up to 1800 bps.

signals.name: STANAG 4539
signals.description: STANAG 4539 or MIL-STD-188-110B/C Appendix C is a HDR (110B) / MDR (110C) serial PSK/QAM signal that can reach speeds up to 9600 bps (12800 bps with no interleaving).

signals.name: STANAG 5065
signals.description: STANAG 5065 is defined as "Minimum Standards for Naval Low Frequency (LF) Shore-To-Ship Surface Broadcast Systems", with two primary protocols, FSK75 and MSK300.

signals.name: STP403 Bus PIT System
signals.description: STP403 is a bus PIT system used to update digital displays at bus stops. STP403 was developed by French companies INEO and CESATEC.

signals.name: SuperDARN (Super Dual Auroral Radar Network)
signals.description: SuperDARN (Super Dual Auroral Radar Network) is an international radar network used for scientific purposes. The network is used to study plasma convection in the upper atmosphere.

signals.name: Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA)
signals.description: Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA) is a control system architecture that is used in industrial applications for computerized automated systems. Wireless telemetry is used on RTU's to send data to control units for operators to utilize.

signals.name: SWED-ARQ
signals.description: SWED-ARQ, also known as ARQ-SWE, was a Swedish simplex ARQ system used by Swedish diplomatic services. This protocol supported three packet lengths and was able to change packet length mid-transmission. No longer used today.

signals.name: Switching Electronic Interference
signals.description: Commonly experienced interfering RF emissions from switching electronics (i.e. switched-mode power supplies, power converters, digital electronics, etc.) which use inductors (coils) that unintentionally act as antennas.

signals.name: System Fusion (C4FM)
signals.description: Yaesu amateur C4FM digital voice.

signals.name: Tactical Air Navigation System (TACAN)
signals.description: Radio navigation technology that measures the slant range (distance) between an aircraft and a ground station by timing the propagation delay of radio signals.

signals.name: TDF
signals.description: TDF, also known as ALS162, is a time signal transmitted on the former carrier of France's '''France Inter''' longwave AM radio station on 162 kHz.

signals.name: Terrestrial Trunked Radio (TETRA)
signals.description: TETRA is a professional mobile radio and two-way transceiver (walkie-talkie) specification

signals.name: Tetrapol
signals.description: Tetrapol is a digital professional mobile radio standard for digital voice and data communication used by public safety and military throughout Europe. Tetrapol was originally developed by Matra Communication (Currently part of EADS/Airbus Group) in France in the 1980's.

signals.name: Thales SALAMANDRE (HFXL)
signals.description: Thales SALAMANDRE (using HFXL waveform) uses up to 16 separate contiguous or not-contiguous narrowband HF channels for high datarate military and tactical communications. Operates on a modified STANAG-4539 platform.

signals.name: Thales Système 3000 HF Modem
signals.description: Thales Système 3000 is a HF modem capable of many different modes of transmission. It has a unique preamble and format to it's signals.

signals.name: Thales Système 3000 Skyhopper
signals.description: Thales Système 3000 Skyhopper is the frequency hopping mode of the Système 3000 Modem. Characterized by it's very short bursts and frequency hopping behavior.

signals.name: Thales Système 3000 Voice Scrambler
signals.description: Voice Scrambling mode from Thales Système 3000 HF Modem. Has characteristic PSK and MFSK bursts at the beginning and end of a voice transmission.

signals.name: The 'Air Horn'
signals.description: "The Air Horn" is a Russian military commandment network serving the Western Military District, which also serves the same purpose as the buzzer. It was first heard in 2017, broadcasting on 4020 kHz. 2 years later, in 2019, it changed to broadcast instead on 4070 kHz (for about 2

signals.name: The Alarm
signals.description: Channel marker of a Russian military station nicknamed "The Alarm". "The Alarm" is a Russian military commandment network serving the Western Military District. So far, apart from test counts, it has not been heard with any actual traffic.

signals.name: The Buzzer (ZhUOZ MDZhB UZB76)
signals.description: The Buzzer, call-sign NZhTI (formerly ANVF, ZhUOZ, MDZhB and UZB-76), is a Russian Military Commandment system signal used to broadcast diplomatic ciphered messages known as "monolit" to the russian navy. If there is no message to broadcast, its "homing" signal is a loud ship-hor

signals.name: The Goose
signals.description: "The Goose" is a Russian military commandment network serving the Western Military District. It broadcasts on 4310 kHz during daytime, changing to 3243 kHz for nighttime.

signals.name: The Pip
signals.description: The Pip is the nickname given by radio listeners to a shortwave radio station that broadcasts on the frequency 5448 kHz by day, and 3756 kHz during the night. It broadcasts short, repeated beeps at a rate of around 50 per minute, for 24 hours per day. The beep signal is occasiona

signals.name: THOR
signals.description: THOR is an adaptation of DominoEX with MFSK16 binary varicode and FEC.

signals.name: THROB
signals.description: THROB is a unique data mode that relies heavily on DSP techniques, using MFSK and AM modulation techniques together.

signals.name: Tire Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS)
signals.description: TPMS (Tire-Pressure Monitoring System), more specifically Direct TPMS (dTPMS), is a system that uses pressure sensors to monitor tire pressure on vehicles.

signals.name: Total Access Communication System (TACS)
signals.description: A first generation analogue mobile cellular system which operated in the United Kingdom and a handful of other countries in Europe. It is also the EU's form of AMPS.

signals.name: Toyota Car Key
signals.description: Wireless entry rolling code car key.

signals.name: Traffic Light Control R09
signals.description: AFSK Modulated signal with 2400Baud for traffic light control. Contains R09.16 telegrams as specified per VDV Standard 420.

signals.name: Transit 5B-5
signals.description: Transit 5B-5, a former TRANSIT navigation satellite, is the oldest satellite known to still transmit a signal. Considered "dead" because its navigational systems failed after 19 days of operation, it still emits a telemetry signal when illuminated.

signals.name: TT2300
signals.description: TT2300, also known as TT2300B, TT2300-ARQ, TRA-2300, and TPLEX, is an 8MFSK synchronous system developed by Thrane & Thrane of Denmark (acquired by UK defense firm Cobham in 2012).

signals.name: TV Satellite Telemetry
signals.description: These signals are narrowband technical carriers transmitted by the Thor‑5 satellite in the Ku‑band, close to 11700 MHz. They are part of the satellite’s TT&C (Telemetry, Tracking and Command) and beacon system.

signals.name: TWINPLEX
signals.description: TWINPLEX, also known as F7B4 and TWINPLEX-SITOR, was a diplex 4-FSK ARQ mode developed by Mackay Radio and Telegraph Company, based in New York City, in the early 1950's. TWINPLEX was used by Interpol, the United Nations, and other diplomatic services.

signals.name: UHF Paging
signals.description: Generic UHF paging carriers (POCSAG/FLEX mixed).

signals.name: UHF Vehicle Location System
signals.description: UHF Vehicle Location System

signals.name: UIC 751-3
signals.description: The UIC radio is an analogue radio, which consists of lineside and mobile (trainborne) equipment. Radio systems following this basic subset allow for simplex and duplex voice communication and use of operating signals (tones), and for selective calls and for data transmission.

signals.name: UK AM Data System (UK-AMDS)
signals.description: UK AM Data System (UK-AMDS) was developed by BBC Research and Development in 1984 as a way to transmit low bitrate data on BBC Radio 4's LF AM carrier. Elements of this system were adopted into ETSI's AMSS.

signals.name: UK GOV MIL WINDRM51
signals.description: UK GOV/MIL "WinDRM51" variant. Unknown purpose, But link between UK & Cyprus has been found some years ago.

signals.name: Ultra Low Latency (ULL) Electronic Trading Network
signals.description: A 48k or 24k baud OQPSK signal that is strongly suspected (through numerous circumstantial pieces of evidence) to be either an experimental or active P2P RF link between financial market data centers, used for High Frequency Trading (HFT) and other latency-sensitive market activi

signals.name: UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) Time Standard
signals.description: UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) time standard transmission from NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) stations WWV in Fort Collins, Colorado USA (2.5, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 MHz) and WWVH in Kauai, Hawaii (2.5, 5, 10, 15 MHz).

signals.name: Vaisala RS41-SG Weather Balloon (Radiosonde)
signals.description: Weather balloon (radiosonde) telemetry data.

signals.name: Vaisala RS80
signals.description: Valsala Radiosonde RS80. This is an analog weather balloon radiosonde. Measures Temperature, Pressure and Humidity.

signals.name: Vaisala RS92-KL Weather Balloon (Radiosonde)
signals.description: RS92-KL and RS92-K are analog radiosondes built by Vaisala in Finland. These radiosondes are used for weather balloons.

signals.name: Vaisala RS92-SGP Weather Balloon (Radiosonde)
signals.description: Weather balloon (radiosonde) telemetry data.

signals.name: VARA HF
signals.description: VARA HF is a sound-card mode used to exchange traffic (Mostly Winlink traffic) on the HF bands

signals.name: VDEW
signals.description: VDEW is a 5-tone selcall mode defined by the Vereinigung Deutscher Elektrizitaetswerke in Germany.

signals.name: Vehicle Counting System
signals.description: Data transmitted from a vehicle counting system installed in car parks. The data is frequency hopping over 10 MHz.

signals.name: VEZHA-S
signals.description: Two-way 100 Bd/500 Hz Russian Telegraph system, attributed name VEZHA-C (Tower-S), usage claimed to be by Russian Ministry of Communications (MinComSvyaz Rossii). Possible usage in meteorology under callsign RWD59.

signals.name: VHF Airband Voice
signals.description: Civil aviation AM voice, 118–137 MHz.

signals.name: VHF Data Link - Mode 2 (VDL-M2)
signals.description: VDL-M2 (Known as VDL2 or VDLM2) is a means of sending information between aircraft and ground stations. signals.name: VHF Omnidirectional Range (VOR)
signals.description: A type of radio navigation system used by aircraft. It is distinctive in that the center frequency is flanked by two FM waves.

signals.name: Vietnamese Siren Jammer
signals.description: Used to interrupt AM boardcast stations such as Radio Free Asia, Radio Đáp Lời Song Núi as well as Radio Sweden.

signals.name: VISEL
signals.description: VISEL, also known as YUG-MIL 120.9 Bd, FEC-12, and YUG-MIL FEC, is a synchronous teleprinter system used by the former Yugoslav military. No longer active today.

signals.name: Visonic MCT-201
signals.description: MCT-201 is a Miniature Pendant PowerCode Wireless Transmitter by Visonic. It is designed for emergency and control applications in wireless security systems, and home automation and remote control systems.

signals.name: VOICE
signals.description: VOICE is a MFSK mode developed by Patrick Lindecker F6CTE in 2006, and was derived from Olivia. It was designed for blind or partially sighted amateur radio operators.

signals.name: Voice Inversion Scrambling
signals.description: Analog Voice Inversion Scrambling divides the spectra into multiple bands and swaps them.

signals.name: WEFAX
signals.description: Radiofax (Also known as Weatherfax, HF-FAX, WEFAX, and Weather Facsimile) is a slow scan analog image transmission mode used for the transmission of weather charts and meteorological reports.

signals.name: Wettersonde E084 (Radiosonde)
signals.description: The E084 is a radiosonde designed in 1990 by Deutsche Wetterdienst. It broadcasts a temperature reading at 403.05 MHz via a FM-modulated tone which changes pitch depending on the temperature.

signals.name: WinDRM
signals.description: WinDRM is an amateur radio derivation of the Digital Radio Mondiale (DRM) digital voice and data transmission protocol. Also known as HamDRM, and Digital SSTV.

signals.name: Wireless Temperature Sensor
signals.description: The freezer temperature is requested by a master at regular intervals, and the slave attached to a freezer responds. The communication format appears to be a variant of chirp spread spectrum, (although the spectrum it consumes is quite narrow at ~150 kHz).

signals.name: WSPR
signals.description: Weak Signal Propagation Reporter.

signals.name: WWV / WWVH
signals.description: NIST HF time and frequency standard stations.

signals.name: WWVB
signals.description: WWVB is the lowest frequency time signal in the USA.

signals.name: Yachta T-219 Voice Scrambler
signals.description: Yachta or Yakhta (Russian for 'Boat') T-219 is an analogue voice scrambler. It is unique in that an FSK sync signal is transmitted in the middle of the main signal, with the scrambled voice stream split above and below the FSK signal.

signals.name: Yaesu System Fusion
signals.description: System Fusion is Yaesu's digital voice/data protocol for amateur radio, using the AMBE+2 vocoder on a C4FM signal.

signals.name: Yugoslavian 16-Tone Modem
signals.description: The Yugoslavian 16-Tone Modem, also known as YUG-Diplo 16-Tone, is a 16 tone OFDM PSK modem used in former Yugoslavia for diplomatic use. No longer used today.

signals.name: Yugoslavian 20-Tone Modem
signals.description: The Yugoslavian 20-Tone Modem, also known as YUG-MIL 20-Tone and YUG Diplo 20-Tone, is a 20 tone OFDM PSK modem used in former Yugoslavia for military and diplomatic use. No longer used today.

signals.name: Zaliv52
signals.description: Military shortwave station broadcasting from the Western Military District in Russia. First heard in March 2017, this station has no channel marker, and it mainly broadcasts Monolith type messages and "MOLNIYA 5X" (МОЛНИЯ 5X) messages addressed to "Zaliv52" (Залив52).

signals.name: Zigbee
signals.description: Zigbee is a low-power, low-data-rate, low-latency mesh network, based on the IEEE 802.15.4 LR-WPAN standard. It is commonly used for automation and IoT devices, including sensors, light switches/bulbs, and other wireless-controlled devices.

signals.name: ZVEI Selcall
signals.description: ZVEI is a family of selcall modes defined by the Zentralverband der Electrotechnischen Industrie in Germany. Selcall modes include ZVEI-1, ZVEI-2, ZVEI-3, PZVEI, DZVEI, PDZVEI and ZVEI-VDEW.
